Moltemplate is a general cross-platform text-based molecule builder for LAMMPS (Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator). It provides a template-based system for creating complex molecular models and preparing molecular dynamics simulations. Moltemplate was designed primarily for building custom coarse-grained molecular models but can also be used for realistic all-atom simulations.

This document provides a high-level overview of Moltemplate's architecture, key components, and workflow. It explains how Moltemplate converts molecule definitions in the LT format (LAMMPS-Template) into LAMMPS input scripts and data files that can be used to run molecular dynamics simulations.

Sources: [README.md:18-43](), [setup.py:38-40]()

## Core Architecture

Moltemplate follows a modular design that allows users to build complex molecular systems from simpler components. At the heart of the system is a template processing engine that handles hierarchical molecule definitions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Core Components"
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"] --> ttree["Template Processing Engine\n(ttree.py/lttree.py)"]
        ttree --> ttree_render["Template Rendering\n(ttree_render.py)"]
        ttree --> ttree_matrix["Matrix Operations\n(ttree_matrix_stack.py)"]
        ttree --> ttree_lex["Template Lexing\n(ttree_lex.py)"]
        ttree --> lttree_post["Post Processing\n(lttree_postprocess.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Input Sources"
        lt_files["LT Files\n(Molecule Definitions)"] --> moltemplate
        pdb["PDB Files"] --> moltemplate
        xyz["XYZ Files"] --> moltemplate
        dump["LAMMPS Dump Files"] --> moltemplate
        raw["Raw Coordinates"] --> moltemplate
    end

    subgraph "Output Files"
        moltemplate --> data["system.data\n(LAMMPS Data File)"]
        moltemplate --> in_init["system.in.init\n(Initialization)"]
        moltemplate --> in_settings["system.in.settings\n(Parameters)"]
        moltemplate --> in_charges["system.in.charges\n(Atomic Charges)"]
    end
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:1-100](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:127-135](), [setup.py:70-104]()

## Conversion and Import Tools

Moltemplate includes a suite of tools for converting various molecule file formats into the LT format, making it interoperable with many existing molecular modeling tools and databases.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "External Formats"
        mol2["MOL2 Files"]
        pdb["PDB Files"]
        xyz["XYZ Files"]
        amber["AMBER/GAFF Files"]
        msi["MSI/FRC Files"]
        lammps_data["LAMMPS Data Files"]
        lammps_input["LAMMPS Input Scripts"]
    end

    subgraph "Conversion Tools"
        mol22lt["mol22lt.py"]
        amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
        msifrc2lt["msifrc2lt.py"]
        ltemplify["ltemplify.py"]
    end

    subgraph "Moltemplate Core"
        lt_files["LT Files\n(Molecule Definitions)"]
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
    end

    mol2 --> mol22lt
    amber --> amber2lt
    msi --> msifrc2lt
    lammps_data --> ltemplify
    lammps_input --> ltemplify
    pdb --> moltemplate
    xyz --> moltemplate
    
    mol22lt --> lt_files
    amber2lt --> lt_files
    msifrc2lt --> lt_files
    ltemplify --> lt_files
    
    lt_files --> moltemplate
```

Sources: [README.md:94-118](), [moltemplate/ltemplify.py:1-30](), [setup.py:85-90]()

## Molecule Building Workflow

A typical workflow with Moltemplate involves defining molecules or molecular fragments in LT format, arranging them in space, and generating simulation files for LAMMPS.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Moltemplate as "moltemplate.sh"
    participant LAMMPS
    participant Visualization as "Visualization Tools (VMD/OVITO)"
    
    User->>Moltemplate: Define molecules in LT format
    User->>Moltemplate: Run moltemplate.sh with parameters
    Moltemplate->>Moltemplate: Process templates
    Moltemplate->>Moltemplate: Resolve variables
    Moltemplate->>Moltemplate: Generate coordinates
    Moltemplate->>User: Create LAMMPS data file
    Moltemplate->>User: Create LAMMPS input scripts
    User->>LAMMPS: Run simulation
    LAMMPS->>User: Generate trajectory
    User->>Visualization: Visualize results
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:127-209](), [README.md:122-126]()

## Template Processing System

The template processing system is the core of Moltemplate's functionality. It handles the interpretation of LT files, resolves variable references, and generates the appropriate LAMMPS files.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Template Processing"
        LT_File["LT File"] --> Parser["Parser\n(ttree_lex.py)"]
        Parser --> Variables["Variable Resolution"]
        Parser --> WriteCommands["write() and write_once() Commands"]
        Variables --> Counter["Counter Variables ($)"]
        Variables --> Category["Category Variables (@)"]
        WriteCommands --> OutputFiles["Output File Fragments"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-Processing"
        OutputFiles --> Assembly["File Assembly\n(lttree_postprocess.py)"]
        Assembly --> NBody["N-body Interactions\n(nbody_by_type.py)"]
        Assembly --> ChargeByBond["Charge Assignment\n(charge_by_bond.py)"]
        Assembly --> Reordering["Atom Reordering\n(nbody_reorder_atoms.py)"]
    end
    
    NBody --> FinalFiles["Final LAMMPS Files"]
    ChargeByBond --> FinalFiles
    Reordering --> FinalFiles
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:127-164](), [setup.py:77-104]()

## LT File Format and Capabilities

The LT (LAMMPS-Template) file format is the native format used by Moltemplate for defining molecules and force fields. It contains all the information relevant to a particular molecule, including coordinates, bond topology, force-field parameters, and constraints.

| Section | Description | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| Molecule Definition | Defines a new molecule type | `Ethane { ... }` |
| Atom Definition | Defines atoms in the molecule | `write("Data Atoms") { $atom:C1 $mol @atom:C 0.0 1.1 2.2 3.3 }` |
| Bond Definition | Defines bonds between atoms | `write("Data Bonds") { $bond:1 @bond:CC $atom:C1 $atom:C2 }` |
| Force Field Parameters | Defines force field parameters | `write_once("In Settings") { pair_coeff @atom:C @atom:C lj/cut 0.066 3.5 }` |
| Hierarchical Structure | Allows molecules to inherit properties | `Ethane inherits OPLSAA { ... }` |
| Coordinate Manipulation | Allows moving, rotating molecules | `move(0.0, 0.0, 5.0)` |

Sources: [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex:167-208](), [doc/doc_ltemplify.md:130-162]()

## Force Fields and Models Support

Moltemplate supports a wide range of force fields and molecular models, allowing users to choose appropriate parameters for their specific simulation needs.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Force Fields"
        OPLSAA["OPLSAA/2023"]
        LOPLS["LOPLS/2015"]
        AMBER["AMBER (GAFF, GAFF2)"]
        DREIDING["DREIDING"]
        COMPASS["COMPASS"]
        MARTINI["MARTINI (Coarse-Grained)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Water Models"
        TIP3P["TIP3P"]
        TIP5P["TIP5P"]
        SPC["SPC/E"]
        mW["mW (Monatomic Water)"]
        ELBA["ELBA Water"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Specialized Models"
        oxDNA["oxDNA2"]
        EFF["EFF (Explicit Electrons)"]
        MOLC["MOLC"]
        TraPPE["TraPPE (1998)"]
    end
    
    OPLSAA --> WaterCompat["Compatible with\nStandard Water Models"]
    AMBER --> WaterCompat
    WaterCompat --> TIP3P
    WaterCompat --> TIP5P
    WaterCompat --> SPC
    
    MOLC --> SpecializedSim["Specialized\nSimulations"]
    oxDNA --> SpecializedSim
    EFF --> SpecializedSim
```

Sources: [README.md:25-42](), [moltemplate/force_fields/oplsaa.lt:1-30](), [moltemplate/force_fields/loplsaa.lt:1-30]()

## Utility Tools

Moltemplate includes several utility tools that enhance its functionality and provide additional capabilities for building complex molecular systems.

| Tool | Purpose | Key Features |
|------|---------|--------------|
| `genpoly_lt.py` | Generate polymer structures | Creates chains, helices, and custom shapes |
| `ltemplify.py` | Convert LAMMPS to LT format | Extracts molecule definitions from existing simulations |
| `mol22lt.py` | Convert MOL2 to LT format | Imports molecular structures from MOL2 files |
| `charge_by_bond.py` | Assign charges | Automatically assigns charges based on bond topology |
| `nbody_by_type.py` | Generate N-body interactions | Creates angle, dihedral, and improper interactions |
| `cleanup_moltemplate.sh` | Clean up output files | Removes temporary files |

Sources: [setup.py:77-104](), [moltemplate/ltemplify.py:1-30](), [README.md:60-62]()

## All-Atom and Coarse-Grained Capabilities

Moltemplate can be used for both all-atom simulations with realistic force fields and coarse-grained simulations with simplified molecular models.

### All-Atom Simulations

For all-atom simulations, users typically need to:
1. Select an appropriate force field (e.g., OPLSAA, AMBER, DREIDING)
2. Define atomic structures with correct atom types
3. Assign partial charges (via force field rules or external tools)
4. Define bonded interactions

Moltemplate can use external sources for atom typing and charge assignment:
- ATB database (provides ready-to-use LT format files)
- AmberTools (generates MOL2 files)
- RED-server (calculates partial charges)
- LigParGen (creates LAMMPS data files)

### Coarse-Grained Simulations

For coarse-grained simulations, Moltemplate allows users to:
1. Define custom interaction sites representing groups of atoms
2. Create custom force fields with simplified potentials
3. Build complex multi-scale models combining all-atom and coarse-grained representations

Sources: [README.md:83-118](), [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex:79-118]()

## Practical Usage and Installation

Moltemplate requires Python (3.4+), NumPy, and BASH to run. It can run on MacOS, Linux, or Windows (with appropriate shell environment).

Typical usage:
```
moltemplate.sh [-atomstyle style] [-pdb/-xyz coord_file] [-vmd] system.lt
```

Installation options:
1. Using pip: `pip3 install moltemplate`
2. Using conda: `conda install conda-forge::moltemplate`
3. Manual installation from GitHub: Clone repository, then run `pip3 install .`

Memory requirements scale with system size:
- 1,000,000 atoms typically requires 3-12 GB of available memory
- Memory usage depends on number of bonds, molecules, and angular interactions

Sources: [README.md:128-146](), [INSTALL.md:1-62](), [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex:137-142]()

## Integration with LAMMPS and Visualization Tools

Moltemplate generates files that can be directly used with LAMMPS for molecular dynamics simulations and is compatible with various visualization tools.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Moltemplate Output"
        data["system.data\n(Molecular Structure)"]
        init["system.in.init\n(Force Field Setup)"]
        settings["system.in.settings\n(Simulation Parameters)"]
        charges["system.in.charges\n(Atomic Charges)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "LAMMPS Simulation"
        lammps["LAMMPS Executor"]
        traj["Trajectory Files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        vmd["VMD"]
        ovito["OVITO"]
        topotools["Topotools"]
    end
    
    data --> lammps
    init --> lammps
    settings --> lammps
    charges --> lammps
    
    lammps --> traj
    traj --> vmd
    traj --> ovito
    data --> vmd
    vmd --> topotools
```

Sources: [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex:298-316](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/hexadecane/run.in.npt:1-109]()

This page provides detailed instructions for installing Moltemplate on different operating systems. Moltemplate is a system designed to simplify the creation of complex molecular simulations for the LAMMPS molecular dynamics software.

## Prerequisites

Before installing Moltemplate, you need to have the following software installed on your system:

- BASH shell
- Python 3
- pip (Python package manager)

Sources: [INSTALL.md:4-6](), [INSTALL.md:61-64]()

## Installation Methods

There are two ways to install Moltemplate:

1. Using pip (recommended)
2. Editing your .bashrc file

It is important to use only one method, not both.

Sources: [INSTALL.md:17-21]()

### Installation Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Installation"]
    Prerequisites["Install Prerequisites:
    - BASH
    - Python 3
    - pip"]
    Download["Download Moltemplate Repository"]
    Decision{"Choose Installation
    Method"}
    PipInstall["Install with pip"]
    BashrcInstall["Edit .bashrc PATH"]
    Verify["Verify Installation"]
    End["Installation Complete"]

    Start --> Prerequisites
    Prerequisites --> Download
    Download --> Decision
    Decision -- "Method 1" --> PipInstall
    Decision -- "Method 2" --> BashrcInstall
    PipInstall --> Verify
    BashrcInstall --> Verify
    Verify --> End

    subgraph "Prerequisites"
        OS["Check OS-Specific
        Requirements"]
    end

    Prerequisites --> OS
```

Sources: [INSTALL.md:7-14](), [INSTALL.md:17-21]()

## Method 1: Installation Using pip

This is the recommended installation method, especially if you plan to use Moltemplate with other Python tools.

### Standard Installation

1. Clone the Moltemplate repository or download the ZIP file:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate DESTINATION_DIRECTORY
   ```

2. Navigate to the downloaded directory:
   ```bash
   cd DESTINATION_DIRECTORY
   ```

3. Install using pip:
   ```bash
   pip3 install .              # (or "pip", if pip3 fails)
   ```

4. If the above fails, try installing for a single user:
   ```bash
   pip3 install . --user       # (or "pip", if pip3 fails)
   ```

5. For system-wide installation (on shared computers):
   ```bash
   sudo pip3 install .         # (or "pip", if pip3 fails)
   ```

Sources: [INSTALL.md:24-49](), [.circleci/config.yml:16]()

### Troubleshooting pip Installation

Common issues when installing with pip:

1. **Missing pip**: If pip is not installed, use your system's package manager to install it
2. **Multiple Python versions**: Make sure pip corresponds to the correct Python version
3. **Permission issues**: Use `--user` flag or `sudo` depending on your system

To check which Python and pip versions are installed:
```bash
which python3
which pip3
```

Ensure both commands return paths in the same directory (e.g., both in `/usr/bin/` or both in a path containing `anaconda`).

Sources: [INSTALL.md:52-117]()

### Optional: Using Python Virtual Environment

Using a virtual environment is recommended for clean installation:

```bash
python3 -m venv venv     # (or "virtualenv venv" if that fails)
source venv/bin/activate
pip3 install .           # (or "pip" if that fails)
```

When using a virtual environment, you must activate it before using Moltemplate:
```bash
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate
```

Sources: [INSTALL.md:120-154]()

## Method 2: Editing PATH in Shell Configuration

This method involves manually adding Moltemplate directories to your system's PATH.

### For BASH shell users:

Add these lines to your `~/.bashrc` file:

```bash
export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/moltemplate/moltemplate"
export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/moltemplate/moltemplate/scripts"
```

Alternative locations include `~/.profile` or `~/.bash_profile`.

### For TCSH shell users:

Add these lines to your `~/.cshrc`, `~/.tcshrc`, or `~/.login` file:

```tcsh
setenv PATH "$PATH:$HOME/moltemplate/moltemplate"
setenv PATH "$PATH:$HOME/moltemplate/moltemplate/scripts"
```

After editing, start a new terminal for the changes to take effect.

**Note**: This method is not recommended if you're using software that has Moltemplate as a Python dependency (like "vipster" or "cellpack2moltemplate"), as those programs require Moltemplate to be installed as a Python package.

Sources: [INSTALL.md:158-193]()

## System Integration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Python Environment"
        PythonInterpreter["Python Interpreter"]
        PipPackageManager["pip Package Manager"]
        PythonVirtualEnv["Python Virtual Environment (optional)"]
    end

    subgraph "Moltemplate System"
        MoltemplateMain["moltemplate.sh Script"]
        PythonModules["Python Modules"]
        Scripts["Helper Scripts"]
    end

    subgraph "Shell Environment"
        BashShell["BASH Shell"]
        PathVariable["PATH Environment Variable"]
    end

    PythonInterpreter --> PythonModules
    PipPackageManager -- "Method 1: Installation" --> MoltemplateMain
    PythonVirtualEnv -- "Contains" --> PipPackageManager
    
    PathVariable -- "Method 2: PATH update" --> MoltemplateMain
    BashShell -- "Executes" --> MoltemplateMain
    MoltemplateMain -- "Uses" --> Scripts
    MoltemplateMain -- "Uses" --> PythonModules
```

Sources: [INSTALL.md:61-64](), [.circleci/config.yml:12-17]()

## OS-Specific Installation Guidelines

### Linux

Most Linux distributions include the necessary prerequisites. If pip is not available, install it using your distribution's package manager:

```bash
# For Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install python3-pip

# For Fedora/RHEL/CentOS
sudo dnf install python3-pip
```

Alternatively, you can install Anaconda Python, which includes pip and numpy by default.

Sources: [INSTALL.md:199-212]()

### macOS

You can install the required prerequisites using Homebrew or Xcode:

```bash
# Using Homebrew
brew install python3
```

Anaconda Python is also available for macOS and may provide a more reliable Python environment.

Sources: [INSTALL.md:214-222]()

### Windows

To use Moltemplate on Windows, you'll need to install a BASH shell environment first. Recommended options:

1. **Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2)** - Preferred option
2. **VirtualBox with a Linux distribution** (like Xubuntu)
3. **Hyper-V** (for newer Windows versions)
4. **Cygwin** (for older Windows versions)

You will also need a Unix-style text editor, as Word, Wordpad, and Notepad are not suitable. Options include:
- Graphical editors: Atom, Sublime, Notepad++, VSCode
- Terminal-based editors: vim, emacs, nano, ne, jove

When using WSL2, be careful when editing Linux files with Windows applications as this can cause file corruption.

Sources: [INSTALL.md:224-261]()

## Verification of Installation

To verify that Moltemplate has been installed correctly, run the following command:

```bash
moltemplate.sh -h
```

This should display the help information for Moltemplate. If you get a "command not found" error, the installation was not successful.

You can also check if the Python module can be imported:

```bash
python3 -c "import moltemplate; print(moltemplate.__file__)"
```

This should print the path to the installed moltemplate module.

Sources: [.circleci/config.yml:16-22]()

## Installation Validation

The Moltemplate testing system verifies installation by running several tests:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Installation Testing"
        Install["Install Moltemplate"]
        Test1["Test PDB Reading"]
        Test2["Test ltemplify"]
        Test3["Test OPLSAA Force Field"]
        Test4["Test COMPASS Force Field"]
        Test5["Test MOLC Format"]
        Test6["Test genpoly_lt"]
    end

    Install --> Test1
    Install --> Test2
    Install --> Test3
    Install --> Test4
    Install --> Test5
    Install --> Test6
```

Sources: [.circleci/config.yml:16-22](), [tests/test_read_coords_pdb.sh:1-34](), [tests/test_ltemplify.sh:1-126](), [tests/test_oplsaa.sh:1-23](), [tests/test_compass.sh:1-22](), [tests/test_molc.sh:1-14]()

## Next Steps

After installation, you can begin creating molecular simulation systems. Moltemplate will generate files for LAMMPS simulations, typically including:

- `system.data` - Contains atom coordinates and molecular topology
- `system.in.init` - Contains initialization parameters
- `system.in.settings` - Contains force field parameters
- `system.in.charges` - Contains atom charges (for some force fields)

These files are used to run simulations in LAMMPS as shown in example run files.

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_OPLSAA/ethylene+benzene/run.in.npt:1-7](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/benzene/run.in.npt:1-7]()

This page outlines the core architecture of moltemplate, explaining the key components that make up the system and how they interact. Moltemplate is a general-purpose template-based molecule builder for LAMMPS that recursively processes template files to generate complex molecular structures and simulation inputs.

For information about molecule building tools like `genpoly_lt.py`, see [Molecule Building Tools](#3). For file format converters, see [File Format Converters](#4).

## System Overview

Moltemplate's architecture follows a layered design centered around template processing. The core engine handles recursive text generation and variable substitution, while specialized components add molecular simulation capabilities.

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "User Interface"
        moltemplate_sh["moltemplate.sh"] --> ttree["ttree.py/lttree.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Template Processing"
        ttree --> ttree_lex["ttree_lex.py"]
        ttree --> ttree_matrix["ttree_matrix_stack.py"]
        ttree --> check["lttree_check.py"]
        ttree --> postprocess["lttree_postprocess.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "N-Body Processing"
        ttree --> nbody["nbody_by_type.py"]
        ttree --> nbody_fix["nbody_fix_ttree_assignments.py"]
        ttree --> nbody_reorder["nbody_reorder_atoms.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Generation"
        ttree --> out_data["DATA files"]
        ttree --> out_settings["IN settings"]
        ttree --> out_init["IN init"]
    end
    
    Input["LT files"] --> moltemplate_sh
    PDB["PDB/XYZ files"] -.-> moltemplate_sh
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:138-225](), [moltemplate/ttree.py:10-44]()

### Component Relationships

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class moltemplate_sh {
        +Process command line args
        +Invoke processing scripts
        +Manage file generation
    }
    
    class ttree {
        +Parse templates
        +Manage variable bindings
        +Process write commands
    }
    
    class lttree {
        +Add LAMMPS-specific handling
        +Process molecule coordinates
        +Handle atom styles
    }
    
    class ttree_lex {
        +Tokenize templates
        +Parse variables
        +Handle quoted strings
    }
    
    class ttree_matrix_stack {
        +Transform coordinates
        +Handle rotations
        +Handle translations
    }
    
    class lttree_check {
        +Validate variable names
        +Verify LAMMPS syntax
    }
    
    class lttree_postprocess {
        +Check for undefined variables
        +Finalize output files
    }
    
    moltemplate_sh --> ttree: invokes
    ttree <|-- lttree: extends
    lttree --> ttree_lex: uses
    lttree --> ttree_matrix_stack: uses
    lttree --> lttree_check: uses
    lttree --> lttree_postprocess: uses
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:127-139](), [moltemplate/ttree.py:126-262](), [moltemplate/lttree.py:31-60]()

## Key Components

### moltemplate.sh

The main script that users directly interact with. It's a bash script that serves as the entry point for moltemplate, parsing command-line arguments and orchestrating the execution of the underlying Python modules.

Key responsibilities:
- Processes command-line arguments
- Checks for dependencies and necessary files
- Invokes the template processing pipeline
- Consolidates output files

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:1-46](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:127-139]()

### ttree.py

The core template processing engine. This module recursively generates text files from template files containing variables and commands.

Key classes:
- `StaticObj`: Stores class definitions and static variables
- `InstanceObj`: Stores instances and their associated variables
- `Command`: Base class for template commands (write, new, etc.)

Key features:
- Variable substitution
- Text template processing
- Command execution

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree.py:10-44](), [moltemplate/ttree.py:109-175]()

### lttree.py

An extension of ttree.py specialized for LAMMPS. Adds molecular simulation specific features like coordinate transformation and atom style handling.

Key additions:
- LAMMPS atom style support
- Coordinate transformation
- Molecular structure handling

Sources: [moltemplate/lttree.py:10-26](), [moltemplate/lttree.py:81-108]()

### ttree_matrix_stack.py

Provides matrix operations for coordinate transformations, supporting operations like rotation and translation of molecular structures.

Key components:
- `AffineTransform`: Performs coordinate transformations
- `MultiAffineStack`: Maintains transformation state
- Matrix multiplication utilities

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree_matrix_stack.py:22-138]()

### lttree_styles.py

Defines LAMMPS-specific styles and data formats, ensuring that the generated output files adhere to LAMMPS conventions.

Key definitions:
- Data file section names
- Input script section names
- Atom style definitions

Sources: [moltemplate/lttree_styles.py:17-61]()

## Template Processing Architecture

The template processing system is the heart of moltemplate, converting high-level molecule descriptions into concrete simulation inputs.

### Template Processing Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Phase"
        LT_File["LT Template File"] --> Tokenizer["Template Tokenizer"]
        Tokenizer --> Parser["Template Parser"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Phase"
        Parser --> Class_Hierarchy["Static Class Hierarchy"]
        Class_Hierarchy --> Instance_Tree["Instance Tree"]
        Instance_Tree --> VarResolver["Variable Resolution"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Phase"
        VarResolver --> FileGen["File Generation"]
        FileGen --> DataFile["LAMMPS Data File"]
        FileGen --> InputScripts["LAMMPS Input Scripts"]
    end
```

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree.py:175-399](), [moltemplate/lttree.py:194-388]()

### Template Variables

Moltemplate uses two key types of variables:

1. **Static variables** (`@variable`): Associated with class definitions
   - Example: `@atom:C`, `@bond:CC`
   - Defined in class scope
   - Typically represent atom types, bond types, etc.

2. **Instance variables** (`$variable`): Associated with specific instances
   - Example: `$atom:C1`, `$bond:b1`
   - Specific to each molecule instance
   - Typically represent specific atoms, bonds, etc.

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree.py:109-147](), [moltemplate/lttree_check.py:109-166]()

## Command Execution Framework

Commands in template files are processed and executed to generate the final output files.

### Command Types

```mermaid
classDiagram
    Command <|-- WriteFileCommand
    Command <|-- InstantiateCommand
    Command <|-- DeleteCommand
    Command <|-- StackableCommand
    StackableCommand <|-- PushCommand
    StackableCommand <|-- PopCommand
    PushCommand <|-- PushRightCommand
    PushCommand <|-- PushLeftCommand
    PopCommand <|-- PopRightCommand
    PopCommand <|-- PopLeftCommand
    
    class Command {
        +srcloc
    }
    
    class WriteFileCommand {
        +filename
        +tmpl_list
    }
    
    class InstantiateCommand {
        +name
        +class_ref
        +instobj
    }
    
    class StackableCommand {
        +context_node
    }
    
    class PushCommand {
        +contents
    }
    
    class PopCommand {
        +partner
    }
```

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree.py:157-390]()

### Command Processing Workflow

The command processing workflow follows a sequential execution model:

1. Template file is parsed into a series of commands
2. Commands are sorted by type and order
3. Static objects (classes) are created and linked
4. Instance commands create the instance hierarchy
5. Write commands populate output files

Sources: [moltemplate/ttree.py:443-520](), [moltemplate/ttree.py:850-914]()

## File Generation

The final step in the process is generating output files for LAMMPS.

### Output File Structure

| File | Purpose | Content |
|------|---------|---------|
| `.data` | LAMMPS data file | Atom coordinates, topology, force field parameters |
| `.in.init` | Initialization script | Force field styles, simulation settings |
| `.in.settings` | Parameter settings | Force field parameters, constraints |
| `.in.charges` | Charge assignments | Atom charge settings |

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:144-184](), [moltemplate/lttree_styles.py:17-61]()

### N-body Interaction Processing

Many-body interactions (angles, dihedrals, impropers) can be automatically generated:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Atoms["Atom Definitions"] --> Bonds["Bond Definitions"]
    Bonds --> nbody_by_type["nbody_by_type.py"]
    nbody_bytype["Data *Bytype"] --> nbody_by_type
    nbody_by_type --> Angles["Angle Definitions"]
    nbody_by_type --> Dihedrals["Dihedral Definitions"]
    nbody_by_type --> Impropers["Improper Definitions"]
```

Sources: [moltemplate/nbody_by_type.py:10-40](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:237-252]()

## Processing Pipeline

The entire moltemplate processing pipeline consists of several sequential steps that transform template files into LAMMPS input files.

### Pipeline Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User
    participant moltemplate as moltemplate.sh
    participant lttree as lttree.py
    participant check as lttree_check.py
    participant postprocess as lttree_postprocess.py
    participant nbody as nbody_by_type.py
    
    User->>moltemplate: LT template file
    moltemplate->>check: Validate templates
    check-->>moltemplate: Validation results
    moltemplate->>lttree: Process templates
    lttree-->>moltemplate: Processed template files
    moltemplate->>postprocess: Post-process files
    postprocess-->>moltemplate: Post-processed files
    moltemplate->>nbody: Process n-body interactions
    nbody-->>moltemplate: Generated interactions
    moltemplate->>User: LAMMPS data and input files
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:901-961]()

## Error Handling

Moltemplate includes a comprehensive error handling system to catch common mistakes:

1. **Syntax validation**: Performed by `lttree_check.py`
2. **Variable verification**: Performed by `lttree_postprocess.py`
3. **Runtime error messages**: Detailed error messages with line numbers

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:73-89](), [moltemplate/lttree_check.py:89-106]()

## Performance Considerations

The recursive template processing can be memory-intensive for large systems:

- Building a system of 1,000,000 atoms typically requires 3-12GB of memory
- Memory usage depends on the number of bonds, molecules, and interactions
- Performance is primarily limited by memory, not CPU

Sources: [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex:136-142]()

## Usage in Larger System

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "External Tools"
        PDB["PDB Files"]
        XYZ["XYZ Files"]
        MOL2["MOL2 Files"]
        AMBER["AMBER Files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate System"
        PDB --> moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
        XYZ --> moltemplate
        MOL2 --> converter["mol22lt.py"]
        AMBER --> amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
        converter --> lt_file["LT Files"]
        amber2lt --> lt_file
        lt_file --> moltemplate
    end
    
    subgraph "LAMMPS System"
        moltemplate --> data["system.data"]
        moltemplate --> in_init["system.in.init"]
        moltemplate --> in_settings["system.in.settings"]
        data --> lammps["LAMMPS Simulator"]
        in_init --> lammps
        in_settings --> lammps
    end
```

Sources: [README.md:88-96](), [setup.py:70-104]()

This diagram shows how moltemplate fits into the broader molecular simulation workflow, connecting multiple input formats to the LAMMPS simulator.

# Page: moltemplate.sh Script

# moltemplate.sh Script

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [doc/doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md)
- [doc/moltemplate_manual_README.md](doc/moltemplate_manual_README.md)
- [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex](doc/moltemplate_manual_src/moltemplate_manual.tex)
- [doc/moltemplate_manual_src/refs.bib](doc/moltemplate_manual_src/refs.bib)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/loplsaa_ext.prm](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/loplsaa_ext.prm)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/loplsaa.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/loplsaa.lt)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/oplsaa.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/oplsaa.lt)
- [moltemplate/ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py)
- [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh](moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh)
- [setup.py](setup.py)

</details>



The `moltemplate.sh` script is the primary entry point for the Moltemplate system. This script converts molecule definition files (`.lt` files) into LAMMPS-compatible data and input script files for molecular simulations. It acts as a wrapper that coordinates various Python scripts for template processing and handles different input formats for molecular coordinates.

For information about the template processing system that moltemplate.sh uses, see [Template Processing System](#2.2).

## Purpose and Functionality

The `moltemplate.sh` script serves as the command-line interface for Moltemplate users. Its main functions include:

1. Processing Moltemplate template (`.lt`) files
2. Converting them into LAMMPS-compatible inputs
3. Incorporating coordinates from external files (PDB, XYZ, DUMP, RAW)
4. Handling various command-line options for customizing the conversion process

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:1-47](), [README.md:123-125]()

## System Architecture

The `moltemplate.sh` script is positioned at the core of the Moltemplate system, orchestrating the conversion of molecular templates into LAMMPS input files.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Moltemplate CLI"
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Processing"
        ttree["ttree.py"]
        lttree["lttree.py"]
        lttree_check["lttree_check.py"]
        lttree_postprocess["lttree_postprocess.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input"
        lt["LT Files"]
        coords["Coordinate Files\n(PDB/XYZ/DUMP/RAW)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        data["system.data"]
        in_init["system.in.init"]
        in_settings["system.in.settings"]
        in_coords["system.in.coords"]
    end
    
    lt --> moltemplate
    coords --> moltemplate
    moltemplate --> ttree
    moltemplate --> lttree
    moltemplate --> lttree_check
    moltemplate --> lttree_postprocess
    ttree --> data
    lttree --> data
    lttree_postprocess --> data
    lttree_postprocess --> in_init
    lttree_postprocess --> in_settings
    lttree_postprocess --> in_coords
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:126-135](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:946-962]()

## Script Organization

The script follows a logical organization structure:

1. **Initialization**: Sets up environment, checks for Python, and locates necessary script files
2. **Command-line Processing**: Parses user inputs and sets appropriate variables
3. **Coordinate Processing**: Extracts atomic coordinates from input files if specified
4. **Template Processing**: Executes the template processing pipeline
5. **Output Generation**: Creates LAMMPS data and input script files

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant moltemplate.sh as "moltemplate.sh"
    participant lttree as "lttree.py"
    participant postprocess as "lttree_postprocess.py"
    participant LAMMPS as "LAMMPS Files"
    
    User->>moltemplate.sh: Run with .lt file and options
    Note over moltemplate.sh: Check dependencies
    Note over moltemplate.sh: Process arguments
    
    alt Coordinate file provided
        User->>moltemplate.sh: -pdb/-xyz/-dump/-raw file
        moltemplate.sh->>moltemplate.sh: Extract coordinates
    end
    
    moltemplate.sh->>lttree: Execute with processed args
    lttree->>moltemplate.sh: Generate file fragments
    moltemplate.sh->>postprocess: Post-process fragments
    postprocess->>LAMMPS: Create DATA and INPUT files
    moltemplate.sh->>User: Report completion
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:15-46](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:456-887](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:946-962]()

## Command-Line Options

The script supports numerous command-line options for customizing the conversion process:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-atomstyle style` | Specify LAMMPS atom style (default: "full") |
| `-pdb file` | Use coordinates from a PDB file |
| `-xyz file` | Use coordinates from an XYZ file |
| `-dump file` | Use coordinates from a LAMMPS dump file |
| `-raw file` | Use coordinates from a RAW file (3-column X Y Z format) |
| `-a "var value"` | Customize atom/bond/angle/dihedral/improper type assignments |
| `-b assignments.txt` | Similar to -a but without ensuring unique values |
| `-nocheck` | Bypass syntax and naming convention checks |
| `-checkff` | Check if valid angle/dihedral interactions exist for bonded atoms |
| `-overlay-bonds` | Allow multiple bonds between the same atoms |
| `-overlay-angles` | Allow multiple angles for the same triplet of atoms |
| `-overlay-dihedrals` | Allow multiple dihedrals for the same quartet of atoms |
| `-overlay-impropers` | Allow multiple impropers for the same quartet of atoms |
| `-overlay-all` | Enable all overlay options |
| `-molc` | Additional processing for "In Settings" file |
| `-lammps-script basename` | Specify the base name for LAMMPS execution script |
| `-run-example` | Append example run section to input script |

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:272-401](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:472-541]()

## Input Processing

The script can process various types of input files to extract atomic coordinates:

### PDB File Processing
The script extracts atom coordinates and optionally periodic boundary information from PDB files. For triclinic cells, it performs the necessary coordinate transformations.

### XYZ File Processing
For XYZ files, the script extracts the atomic coordinates, ignoring the header information.

### DUMP File Processing
When processing LAMMPS dump files, the script extracts coordinates, velocities, quaternions (for ellipsoid particles), and box dimensions.

### RAW File Processing
RAW files are simple 3-column files containing X Y Z coordinates, which are extracted directly.

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:622-638](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:639-676](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:724-808](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:547-558]()

## Output Files

The script generates several output files:

1. **system.data**: LAMMPS data file containing atom coordinates, topology, and force field parameters
2. **system.in.init**: LAMMPS input script for initialization
3. **system.in.settings**: LAMMPS input script for force field settings
4. **system.in.coords**: LAMMPS input script for coordinate settings (optional)
5. **run.in.EXAMPLE**: Example LAMMPS execution script (if `-run-example` is specified)

If a custom base name is specified using `-lammps-script`, the output files will use that name instead of "system".

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:900-905](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:907-933]()

## Error Handling

The script performs several validations:

1. Checks for the availability of Python
2. Verifies that all required script files exist
3. Validates command-line arguments
4. Checks for the existence and validity of input files
5. Reports errors with descriptive messages

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:17-46](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:119-125](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:83-89]()

## Example Usage

Basic usage with a single LT file:
```
moltemplate.sh system.lt
```

Using coordinates from a PDB file:
```
moltemplate.sh -pdb coordinates.pdb system.lt
```

Specifying a custom atom style:
```
moltemplate.sh -atomstyle "full" system.lt
```

Using coordinates and launching VMD for visualization:
```
moltemplate.sh -xyz coords.xyz -atomstyle "full" -vmd system.lt
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:272-401](), [README.md:123-125]()

## Implementation Details

### Python Version Check

The script first checks for Python 3, falling back to Python 2 with a deprecation warning if necessary:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start["Start"] --> checkPython3["Check if python3 is available"]
    checkPython3 -- Yes --> setPython3["Set PYTHON_COMMAND='python3'"]
    checkPython3 -- No --> checkPython["Check if python is available"]
    checkPython -- Yes --> checkVersion["Check Python version"]
    checkVersion -- >= 3 --> setPython["Set PYTHON_COMMAND='python'"]
    checkVersion -- < 3 --> warnPython2["Warn about Python 2.7 deprecation"] --> setPython
    checkPython -- No --> checkPython2["Check if python2 is available"]
    checkPython2 -- Yes --> warnPython2_2["Warn about Python 2.7 deprecation"] --> setPython2["Set PYTHON_COMMAND='python2'"]
    checkPython2 -- No --> error["Exit with error: Python required"]
    setPython3 --> findScripts["Find script directory"]
    setPython --> findScripts
    setPython2 --> findScripts
    error --> end["End"]
    findScripts --> checkDependencies["Check if required scripts exist"]
    checkDependencies -- All found --> continue["Continue execution"]
    checkDependencies -- Missing --> errorDep["Exit with installation error"]
    continue --> end
    errorDep --> end
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:15-46](), [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:119-125]()

### Argument Processing

The script processes command-line arguments through a loop that evaluates each argument and sets the appropriate variables:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    args["Command-line args"] --> loop["Process each argument"]
    loop --> atomstyle["Process -atomstyle"]
    loop --> coordinates["Process -pdb/-xyz/-dump/-raw"]
    loop --> assignments["Process -a/-b"]
    loop --> checks["Process -nocheck/-checkff"]
    loop --> overlay["Process -overlay options"]
    loop --> misc["Process other options"]
    atomstyle --> updateArgs["Update TTREE_ARGS"]
    coordinates --> extractCoords["Extract coordinates"]
    assignments --> setAssignments["Set assignment variables"]
    checks --> setChecks["Set check flags"]
    overlay --> setOverlay["Set overlay flags"]
    misc --> setMisc["Set miscellaneous variables"]
    updateArgs --> next["Process next argument"]
    extractCoords --> next
    setAssignments --> next
    setChecks --> next
    setOverlay --> next
    setMisc --> next
    next --> finished["All arguments processed?"]
    finished -- Yes --> execute["Execute lttree"]
    finished -- No --> loop
```

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:456-887]()

## Conclusion

The `moltemplate.sh` script is the central component of the Moltemplate system that orchestrates the conversion of molecular templates into LAMMPS-compatible input files. It provides a flexible command-line interface with numerous options for customizing the conversion process and supports various input formats for coordinates. Understanding how to use this script effectively is essential for successfully preparing molecular simulations with Moltemplate.

Sources: [moltemplate/scripts/moltemplate.sh:1-47](), [README.md:123-125]()

# Page: Template Processing System

# Template Processing System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [moltemplate/bonds_by_type.py](moltemplate/bonds_by_type.py)
- [moltemplate/charge_by_bond.py](moltemplate/charge_by_bond.py)
- [moltemplate/dump2data.py](moltemplate/dump2data.py)
- [moltemplate/lttree.py](moltemplate/lttree.py)
- [moltemplate/lttree_check.py](moltemplate/lttree_check.py)
- [moltemplate/lttree_postprocess.py](moltemplate/lttree_postprocess.py)
- [moltemplate/lttree_styles.py](moltemplate/lttree_styles.py)
- [moltemplate/nbody_by_type.py](moltemplate/nbody_by_type.py)
- [moltemplate/nbody_by_type_lib.py](moltemplate/nbody_by_type_lib.py)
- [moltemplate/nbody_fix_ttree_assignments.py](moltemplate/nbody_fix_ttree_assignments.py)
- [moltemplate/postprocess_coeffs.py](moltemplate/postprocess_coeffs.py)
- [moltemplate/postprocess_transitions.py](moltemplate/postprocess_transitions.py)
- [moltemplate/raw2data.py](moltemplate/raw2data.py)
- [moltemplate/ttree.py](moltemplate/ttree.py)
- [moltemplate/ttree_lex.py](moltemplate/ttree_lex.py)
- [moltemplate/ttree_matrix_stack.py](moltemplate/ttree_matrix_stack.py)
- [moltemplate/ttree_render.py](moltemplate/ttree_render.py)

</details>



The Template Processing System is the core engine of Moltemplate, responsible for transforming hierarchical molecular definitions into LAMMPS-compatible input files. It provides a powerful framework for building complex molecular systems from reusable components.

This document focuses on the internal architecture and processing flow of the template system. For information about writing templates and using Moltemplate, refer to other sections of the documentation.

## Core Architecture

The Template Processing System consists of several interconnected components that work together to process templates into LAMMPS files:

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserInput[".lt Template Files"] --> Lexer["Template Lexer\n(ttree_lex.py)"]
    Lexer --> Parser["Template Parser\n(ttree.py)"]
    Parser --> StaticTree["Static Objects\n(Class Definitions)"]
    StaticTree --> InstanceTree["Instance Objects\n(Molecule Instances)"]
    InstanceTree --> FileWriter["File Writer\n(LAMMPS Files)"]
    
    StaticTree -.-> Variables["Variable System\n(@static, $instance)"]
    InstanceTree -.-> Variables
    InstanceTree -.-> MatrixStack["Matrix Stack\n(ttree_matrix_stack.py)"]
    
    LttreeExt["LAMMPS Extensions\n(lttree.py)"] -.-> Parser
    LttreeExt -.-> FileWriter
```

Sources: [ttree.py:1-107](), [lttree.py:10-34](), [ttree_matrix_stack.py:1-19]()

## Template Lexical Analysis

The system begins by tokenizing template files using two specialized lexers:

1. **TtreeShlex**: An enhanced version of Python's standard `shlex` module that better handles Unicode characters.
2. **TemplateLexer**: Processes templates to extract variables, commands, and text blocks.

### Key Classes for Lexical Analysis

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class TtreeShlex {
        +instream
        +wordterminators
        +get_token()
        +push_token()
        +sourcehook()
    }
    
    class TemplateLexer {
        +read_template()
        +process_var_refs()
        +handle_file_includes()
    }
    
    class TextBlock {
        +text: String
        +srcloc: SrcLoc
    }
    
    class VarRef {
        +prefix: String
        +descr_str: String
        +suffix: String
        +nptr: VarNPtr
    }
    
    TtreeShlex <|-- TemplateLexer
    TemplateLexer ..> TextBlock
    TemplateLexer ..> VarRef
```

Templates are broken down into alternating `TextBlock` and `VarRef` objects. Variable references (like `@atom:C` or `$bond:b1`) are represented by `VarRef` objects that track their type, name, and location.

Sources: [ttree_lex.py:21-453](), [ttree_lex.py:710-880]()

## Object System

The system builds two tree structures during template processing:

### Static Object Tree

The static tree represents class/template definitions:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Root["Root Static\n(Global Scope)"] --> MolA["MoleculeA\n(StaticObj)"]
    Root --> MolB["MoleculeB\n(StaticObj)"]
    
    MolA --> AtomType1["@atom:C"]
    MolA --> AtomType2["@atom:H"]
    MolA --> BondType["@bond:CH"]
    MolA --> WriteCmd["write('Data Atoms')"]
    
    MolB --> Inherit["inherits from MolA"]
    MolB --> NewAtom["@atom:N"]
    MolB --> CreateCmd["new MolA.move(1,0,0)"]
```

The `StaticObj` class represents molecule types/classes and stores:
- Static variables (`@` variables)
- Commands to execute during instantiation
- Inheritance relationships

### Instance Object Tree

The instance tree represents actual molecule instances:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Root["Root Instance\n(System)"] --> Mol1["MoleculeA[1]\n(InstanceObj)"]
    Root --> Mol2["MoleculeB[1]\n(InstanceObj)"]
    
    Mol1 --> Atom1["$atom:C1"]
    Mol1 --> Atom2["$atom:H1"]
    Mol1 --> Bond["$bond:b1"]
    
    Mol2 --> SubMol["MoleculeA[2]\n(moved)"]
    Mol2 --> Atom3["$atom:N1"]
    
    SubMol --> SubAtom1["$atom:C1"]
    SubMol --> SubAtom2["$atom:H1"]
```

The `InstanceObj` class represents instantiated molecules and stores:
- Instance variables (`$` variables)
- Transformed coordinates
- Hierarchical structure of instances

Sources: [ttree.py:109-151](), [ttree.py:560-896]()

## Command System

Commands control what happens during template processing:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Command["Command\n(Base Class)"] --> WriteFile["WriteFileCommand\nwrite(), write_once()"]
    Command --> Instantiate["InstantiateCommand\nnew Class.move()"]
    Command --> Delete["DeleteCommand\ndelete()"]
    Command --> Stackable["StackableCommand\nTransformations"]
    
    Stackable --> Push["PushCommand"]
    Stackable --> Pop["PopCommand"]
    
    Push --> PushLeft["PushLeftCommand"]
    Push --> PushRight["PushRightCommand"]
    
    Pop --> PopLeft["PopLeftCommand"]
    Pop --> PopRight["PopRightCommand"]
```

### Key Command Types:

1. **WriteFileCommand**: Outputs content to LAMMPS files
   - Generated by `write()` and `write_once()` in templates
   - Handles template rendering and variable substitution

2. **InstantiateCommand**: Creates new instances
   - Generated by `new` commands in templates
   - Creates InstanceObj nodes in the instance tree

3. **StackableCommand**: Manages transformations
   - Includes PushCommand and PopCommand variants
   - Controls the matrix stack for positioning molecules

Sources: [ttree.py:156-446](), [lttree.py:301-419]()

## Variable System

The template system uses two types of variables:

### Static Variables (@)

- Prefixed with `@` (e.g., `@atom:C`, `@bond:CC`)
- Associated with class definitions (StaticObj)
- Shared across all instances of a class
- Often represent atom types, bond types, etc.

### Instance Variables ($)

- Prefixed with `$` (e.g., `$atom:C1`, `$bond:b1`)
- Associated with specific instances (InstanceObj)
- Unique to each instance
- Often auto-generated during instantiation

Variables are resolved following scoping rules that navigate both the static and instance trees.

Sources: [ttree.py:498-558](), [ttree_lex.py:890-1050]()

## Matrix Stack System

The matrix stack system handles the positioning of molecules in 3D space:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Command["move(x,y,z)\nrot(angle,x,y,z)"] --> Parse["CommandsToMatrix()"]
    Parse --> Matrix["4x4 Transformation\nMatrix"]
    Matrix --> Push["Push to Matrix Stack"]
    Push --> Apply["Apply to Coordinates"]
    Apply --> Molecule["Transformed\nMolecule"]
```

### Key Components:

1. **AffineStack**: Manages the transformation stack
   - Maintains current transformation matrix
   - Handles push/pop operations
   - Composes multiple transformations

2. **Transformation Commands**: User-friendly syntax
   - `move(x,y,z)`: Translation
   - `rot(angle,x,y,z)`: Rotation
   - These are converted to transformation matrices

3. **Coordinate Transformation**: Applies matrices to coordinates
   - Transforms atom positions during instantiation
   - Handles hierarchical transformations

Sources: [ttree_matrix_stack.py:29-57](), [ttree_matrix_stack.py:129-372](), [lttree.py:302-362]()

## Template Processing Flow

The entire template processing flow consists of several phases:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User Input
    participant Lexer as Template Lexer
    participant Static as Static Tree
    participant Instance as Instance Tree
    participant Output as LAMMPS Files
    
    User->>Lexer: Template files (.lt)
    Lexer->>Static: Build class definitions
    Static->>Static: Resolve @variables
    Static->>Instance: Execute new commands
    Instance->>Instance: Apply transformations
    Instance->>Instance: Generate $variables
    Instance->>Output: Write LAMMPS files
```

1. **Lexing Phase**:
   - Template files are read and tokenized
   - Variables and commands are identified
   - Basic syntax checking occurs

2. **Static Building Phase**:
   - StaticObj tree is constructed
   - Class hierarchy is established
   - Static variables are assigned
   - Commands are registered

3. **Instantiation Phase**:
   - InstanceObj tree is built
   - Instance variables are generated
   - Transformations are applied
   - Coordinates are calculated

4. **Output Phase**:
   - LAMMPS files are generated
   - Variables are substituted with their values
   - Final files are written to disk

Sources: [ttree.py:606-814](), [lttree.py:606-626]()

## LAMMPS Integration

The `lttree.py` extension adds LAMMPS-specific features to the basic template system:

1. **Atom Style Support**:
   - Understands different LAMMPS atom styles
   - Maps between atom styles and column formats
   - Handles LAMMPS-specific data formats

2. **Coordinate Transformation**:
   - Transforms atomic coordinates and vectors
   - Preserves LAMMPS data structure requirements
   - Handles different atom styles appropriately

3. **Data File Generation**:
   - Creates properly formatted LAMMPS data files
   - Manages sections like "Atoms", "Bonds", "Angles"
   - Generates complete simulation inputs

Sources: [lttree.py:81-111](), [lttree.py:301-362](), [lttree_styles.py:21-81]()

## Template Rendering Process

The rendering process converts template content with variables into final text by substituting variable values:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Template["Template with\nVariables"] --> VarScan["Variable\nScanning"]
    VarScan --> Lookup["Variable Value\nLookup"]
    Lookup --> Substitute["Variable\nSubstitution"]
    Substitute --> FinalText["Rendered\nOutput Text"]
    
    Template --> TextBlock["TextBlock\nObjects"]
    Template --> VarRef["VarRef\nObjects"]
    TextBlock --> FinalText
    VarRef --> Lookup
```

This process:
1. Identifies variables in the template text
2. Looks up their values in the appropriate scope
3. Substitutes the values into the template
4. Generates the final rendered text

The `Render()` function is the core of this process, taking a template and variable bindings and producing rendered text.

Sources: [ttree.py:2565-2632](), [lttree.py:503-602]()

## Debug and Error Handling

The template system includes robust error handling:

1. **InputError**: Custom exception for user-related errors
2. **Error Leaders**: Functions to generate helpful error messages
3. **Source Location Tracking**: Each element knows its source location

Various checks validate:
- Variable existence
- Command syntax
- Tree structure integrity
- LAMMPS compatibility

Sources: [ttree_lex.py:1320-1380](), [lttree_check.py:109-173]()

## Conclusion

The Template Processing System serves as the foundation of Moltemplate, enabling complex molecular systems to be built from hierarchical templates. Understanding its architecture helps users create more effective templates and troubleshoot issues that may arise.

Sources: [ttree.py:10-45](), [lttree.py:10-34]()

---

# Page: Molecule Building Tools

# Molecule Building Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [doc/doc_dump2data.md](doc/doc_dump2data.md)
- [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md](doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md)

- [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md](doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md)
- [doc/doc_raw2data.md](doc/doc_raw2data.md)
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/moltemplate_files/wall.lt](examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/moltemplate_files/wall.lt)
- [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py](moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py)
- [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py](moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py)
- [moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py](moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py)
- [moltemplate/pdbsort.py](moltemplate/pdbsort.py)
- [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py](tests/test_genpoly_lt.py)

</details>



This page documents the specialized tools in moltemplate for building complex molecular structures, particularly polymers and multi-unit systems. These tools bridge the gap between basic molecular components (monomers) and complex structures ready for simulation. For information about file format converters, see [File Format Converters](#4).

## Overview of Molecule Building Tools

Moltemplate provides three primary tools for building complex molecular structures:

1. **genpoly_lt.py**: Generates polymer definitions by placing monomers along specified coordinates
2. **genpoly_modify_lt.py**: Modifies existing polymers by adding/changing bonds or other interactions
3. **interpolate_curve.py**: Creates smooth curves for polymer placement

These tools form a pipeline for creating polymer structures from basic spatial coordinates to LAMMPS-ready format.

### Workflow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Input Preparation"
        raw_coords["Raw Coordinates"]
        monomer["Monomer Definition"]
        sequence["Optional Sequence"]
        bonds["Bond Specifications"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Molecule Building Tools"
        interp["interpolate_curve.py"]
        genpoly["genpoly_lt.py"]
        genpolymod["genpoly_modify_lt.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate Processing"
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
    end
    
    subgraph "LAMMPS Input Files"
        data["system.data"]
        in_files["system.in.*"]
    end
    
    raw_coords --> interp
    interp --> smooth_coords["Smoothed Coordinates"]
    smooth_coords --> genpoly
    monomer --> genpoly
    sequence --> genpoly
    bonds --> genpoly
    
    genpoly --> polymer_lt["Polymer .lt File"]
    polymer_lt --> genpolymod
    
    mod_specs["Modification Specs"] --> genpolymod
    genpolymod --> mod_polymer_lt["Modified Polymer .lt File"]
    
    polymer_lt -- "Optional" --> moltemplate
    mod_polymer_lt --> moltemplate
    
    moltemplate --> data
    moltemplate --> in_files
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:1-766](), [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py:1-306](), [moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py:1-125]()

## genpoly_lt.py

`genpoly_lt.py` is a powerful tool for generating polymer definitions. It reads coordinates from a file and creates a moltemplate (.lt) file containing a polymer molecule with monomers located at those positions. Monomers are rotated to point along the polymer axis with optional helical twist.

### Key Features

- Places monomers at specified 3D coordinates
- Rotates monomers to align with the polymer's direction
- Supports custom monomer sequences (heteropolymers)
- Creates bonds, angles, dihedrals between monomers
- Handles circular polymers and multiple polymer chains
- Allows helical twisting (useful for DNA models)

### Core Components

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GenPoly {
        +settings: GPSettings
        +coords_multi: List
        +name_sequence_multi: List
        +direction_vects: List
        +N: int
        +orientations_multi: List
        +ParseArgs(argv)
        +ReadCoords(infile, ncolumns)
        +ReadSequence(infile)
        +ChooseDirections(coords)
        +WriteLTFile(outfile)
    }
    
    class GPSettings {
        +infile_name: str
        +direction_orig: List
        +is_circular: bool
        +connect_ends: bool
        +delta_phi: float
        +name_monomer: str
        +name_sequence_file: str
        +name_polymer: str
        +inherits: str
        +cuts: List
        +bonds_type: List
        +bonds_atoms: List
        +ParseArgs(argv)
    }
    
    GenPoly "1" -- "1" GPSettings: contains
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:83-425](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:484-515]()

### Command Line Usage

Basic usage:
```
genpoly_lt.py [options] < coords.raw > polymer.lt
```

Important options include:
- `-polymer-name NAME`: Name of the moltemplate object (default: "Polymer")
- `-monomer-name NAME`: Name of the monomer to replicate (default: "Monomer")
- `-sequence FILE`: File with list of monomer types for heteropolymers
- `-bond TYPE ATOM1 ATOM2`: Define bonds between successive monomers
- `-angle TYPE ATOM1 ATOM2 ATOM3 I1 I2 I3`: Define angles between monomers
- `-helix ANGLE`: Rotate each monomer around axis by ANGLE degrees
- `-circular yes/no/connected`: Specify if polymer is circular
- `-cuts FILE`: Cut polymer into multiple separate polymers
- `-header TEXT`: Custom text to add at file beginning (typically imports)

Example creating a DNA polymer:
```
genpoly_lt.py -circular yes -helix 34.2857 \
              -header 'import "basepair.lt"' \
              -monomer-name "BasePair" \
              -polymer-name "Plasmid" \
              -bond Backbone O3p_a P_a \
              -bond Backbone P_b O3p_b \
              < dna_basepair_coords.raw \
              > chromosome.lt
```

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:33-59](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:439-450]()

### Python API

`genpoly_lt.py` can also be used as a Python module:

```python
import moltemplate
import numpy as np

# Create coordinates for polymer
coords = np.array([[i, 0.5*(i%2), 0.0] for i in range(0,21)])

# Create polymer using genpoly_lt
gp = moltemplate.genpoly_lt.GenPoly()
gp.coords_multi = [coords]
gp.name_sequence_multi = [['AT', 'CG', 'GC', 'TA', 'AT', 'CG', 'GC', 'TA',
                           'AT', 'CG', 'GC', 'TA', 'AT', 'CG', 'GC', 'TA',
                           'AT', 'CG', 'GC', 'TA', 'AT']]

# Parse arguments
gp.ParseArgs(['-helix', '34.2857',
              '-bond', 'Backbone', 'f', 'f',
              '-bond', 'Backbone', 'r', 'r',
              '-polymer-name', 'DNA_snippet'])

# Generate LT file
import sys
gp.WriteLTFile(sys.stdout)
```

Sources: [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py:1-44](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:494-538]()

## genpoly_modify_lt.py

`genpoly_modify_lt.py` allows you to modify existing polymers by adding or changing bonds, angles, dihedrals, atom types, or adding constraint fixes at specific locations along the polymer.

### Key Features

- Modify polymers at specific locations
- Add or change bonds between atoms
- Add angle, dihedral, and improper interactions
- Change atom types or other attributes
- Add restraint fixes or twist motors
- Distribute modifications periodically or randomly

### Core Components

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GPModSettings {
        +polymer_name: str
        +N: int
        +connect_ends: bool
        +locations: List
        +nmods: int
        +widths: List
        +occupancy: List
        +gen_locations_method: str
        +bonds_type: List
        +bonds_atoms: List
        +bonds_index_offsets: List
        +angles_type: List
        +angles_atoms: List
        +angles_index_offsets: List
        +LoadModLocations(filename)
        +ParseArgs(argv)
    }
    
    class DistributeLocations {
        +DistributePeriodic(widths, occupancy, is_periodic, offset)
        +DistributeRandom(widths, occupancy, is_periodic, rand_seed)
        +FindNearestAvailableSite(i, width, occupancy, is_periodic)
    }
    
    GPModSettings --> DistributeLocations: uses
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py:66-306](), [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py:334-384]()

### Command Line Usage

Basic usage:
```
genpoly_modify_lt.py [options] >> polymer.lt
```

Important options include:
- `-polymer-name NAME`: Name of the polymer to modify
- `-length NUM`: Total number of monomers in polymer
- `-locations FILE`: File with list of modification locations
- `-locations-periodic NUM OFFSET`: Place NUM modifications at periodic intervals
- `-locations-random NUM SEED`: Place NUM modifications randomly
- `-width WIDTH`: Minimum width of each modification
- `-bond TYPE ATOM1 ATOM2 I1 I2`: Add bond between atoms
- `-angle TYPE ATOM1 ATOM2 ATOM3 I1 I2 I3`: Add angle interaction
- `-set-atoms M FILE ATTR A1...AM I1...IM ATTR1...ATTRM`: Set atom attributes
- `-fix-nbody N FILE FIXNAME FIXID GROUP KW A1...AN I1...IN PARAMS`: Add fix constraint
- `-circular yes/no`: Specify if polymer is circular

Example modifying a DNA polymer:
```
genpoly_modify_lt.py -polymer-name DNA \
                     -length 1000 \
                     -locations-periodic 10 0 \
                     -bond ProteinLink p_attach c_attach 0 1 \
                     >> dna_with_proteins.lt
```

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:44-60](), [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:250-265]()

### Modification Location Methods

`genpoly_modify_lt.py` provides three ways to specify where modifications should be made:

1. **Manual specification**: Provide a file with list of locations
    ```
    genpoly_modify_lt.py -locations locations.txt ...
    ```
   
2. **Periodic placement**: Distribute modifications evenly
    ```
    genpoly_modify_lt.py -locations-periodic 20 5 ...
    ```
   
3. **Random placement**: Distribute modifications randomly
    ```
    genpoly_modify_lt.py -locations-random 15 12345 ...
    ```

When working with multiple types of modifications, care must be taken to prevent overlaps by:
- Using `-write-locations` to save generated locations
- Applying different modification types separately
- Using different seeds for random placement

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:77-102](), [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py:456-474]()

## interpolate_curve.py

`interpolate_curve.py` uses cubic spline interpolation to create smooth curves from a set of control points. This is especially useful for creating paths for polymers to follow.

### Key Features

- Smooths jagged coordinate sets
- Resamples to desired number of points
- Maintains general path shape
- Uses centripetal Catmull-Rom spline interpolation
- Can scale the resulting coordinates

### Core Components

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    input["Input Control Points"] --> spline["CalcNaturalCubicSplineCoeffs()"]
    spline --> coeffs["Spline Coefficients\nc3a, c3b, c1a, c1b, tcontrol"]
    coeffs --> resample["Resample Curve"]
    resample --> output["Smooth, Evenly-Spaced Points"]
    
    subgraph "ResampleCurve() Function"
        spline
        coeffs
        resample
    end
```

Sources: [moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py:65-197](), [moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py:250-277]()

### Command Line Usage

Basic usage:
```
interpolate_curve.py NUM_POINTS [SCALE] [ALPHA] < old_coords.raw > new_coords.raw
```

Where:
- `NUM_POINTS`: Number of points in the output curve
- `SCALE`: Optional scaling factor (default: 1.0)
- `ALPHA`: Interpolation parameter (default: 0.5)

Example:
```
interpolate_curve.py 150000 7.99 < rough_curve.raw > smooth_curve.raw
```

Sources: [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:19-31](), [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:114-117]()

### Python API

`interpolate_curve.py` can also be used as a Python module:

```python
import moltemplate.interpolate_curve as ic
import numpy as np

# Generate a rough curve
x_orig = np.array([[i, 0.5*(i%2), 0.0] for i in range(0,10)])

# Create a smooth version with 500 points
x_new = ic.ResampleCurve(x_orig, 500, 0.5)

# Scale the curve if needed
x_new *= 0.332
```

Sources: [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:145-153](), [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py:7-15]()

## Complete Workflow Example

The following diagram and steps illustrate a typical workflow using these tools to create a polymer that follows a complex path:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "1. Generate Initial Curve"
        ndmansfield["Space-filling Curve\n(e.g., from ndmansfield)"]
        recenter["Center Coordinates\n(recenter_coords.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "2. Smooth and Prepare Curve"
        interpolate["Smooth Curve\n(interpolate_curve.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "3. Generate Polymer"
        genpoly["Create Polymer Definition\n(genpoly_lt.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "4. Modify Polymer (Optional)"
        genpolymod["Add Modifications\n(genpoly_modify_lt.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "5. Process with Moltemplate"
        moltemplate["Generate LAMMPS Files\n(moltemplate.sh)"]
    end
    
    ndmansfield --> recenter
    recenter --> interpolate
    interpolate --> genpoly
    genpoly --> genpolymod
    genpolymod --> moltemplate
    
    monomer["Monomer Definition\n(.lt file)"] --> genpoly
    sequence["Sequence Definition\n(optional)"] --> genpoly
    
    modlocs["Modification Locations"] --> genpolymod
    
    moltemplate --> output["LAMMPS Input Files"]
```

### Example Steps:

1. **Generate Initial Curve**:
   ```bash
   ndmansfield -box 53 40 31 -cyclic yes > curve.raw
   recenter_coords.py 0 0 0 < curve.raw > curve_centered.raw
   ```

2. **Smooth Curve**:
   ```bash
   interpolate_curve.py 150000 7.99 < curve_centered.raw > smooth_curve.raw
   ```

3. **Generate Polymer**:
   ```bash
   genpoly_lt.py -monomer-name "Monomer" \
                 -polymer-name "Polymer" \
                 -bond Backbone C C \
                 -header 'import "monomer.lt"' \
                 < smooth_curve.raw > polymer.lt
   ```

4. **Add Modifications** (optional):
   ```bash
   genpoly_modify_lt.py -polymer-name "Polymer" \
                        -length 150000 \
                        -locations-random 100 12345 \
                        -bond SpecialBond A B 0 1 \
                        >> polymer.lt
   ```

5. **Generate LAMMPS Files**:
   ```bash
   moltemplate.sh -atomstyle "full" polymer.lt
   ```

Sources: [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:100-131](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:425-450](), [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:44-59]()

## Integration with Other Tools

The molecule building tools integrate with other parts of the moltemplate ecosystem:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "External Tools"
        ndmansfield["Space-filling Curve\n(ndmansfield)"]
        lammps["LAMMPS Simulator"]
    end
    
    subgraph "File Format Converters"
        mol22lt["mol22lt.py"]
        amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
        oplsaa2lt["oplsaa2lt.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Molecule Building Tools"
        interpolate["interpolate_curve.py"]
        genpoly["genpoly_lt.py"]
        genpolymod["genpoly_modify_lt.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Moltemplate"
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
    end
    
    ndmansfield --> interpolate
    
    mol22lt --> monomer["Monomer Definitions (.lt)"]
    amber2lt --> monomer
    oplsaa2lt --> monomer
    
    monomer --> genpoly
    interpolate --> genpoly
    genpoly --> polymer["Polymer Definition (.lt)"]
    polymer --> genpolymod
    genpolymod --> modified["Modified Polymer (.lt)"]
    
    polymer --> moltemplate
    modified --> moltemplate
    
    moltemplate --> lammps_files["LAMMPS Input Files"]
    lammps_files --> lammps
```

Sources: [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:56-64](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:13-16]()

## Usage Scenarios

The molecule building tools are particularly useful for:

| Scenario | Recommended Tools |
|----------|-------------------|
| DNA/RNA models | `genpoly_lt.py` with `-helix` option |
| Confined polymers | `interpolate_curve.py` + `genpoly_lt.py` |
| Protein-decorated DNA | `genpoly_lt.py` + `genpoly_modify_lt.py` |
| Branched polymers | `genpoly_lt.py` + `genpoly_modify_lt.py` |
| Heteropolymers | `genpoly_lt.py` with `-sequence` option |
| Circular structures | `genpoly_lt.py` with `-circular yes` |

The tools are especially valuable for coarse-grained models where polymer architecture and topology are essential to the simulation.

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:3-9](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:13-30](), [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:3-40]()
