# Page: genpoly_lt.py - Polymer Generation

# genpoly_lt.py - Polymer Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [doc/doc_dump2data.md](doc/doc_dump2data.md)
- [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md](doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md)
- [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md](doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md)
- [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md](doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md)
- [doc/doc_raw2data.md](doc/doc_raw2data.md)
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/moltemplate_files/wall.lt](examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/moltemplate_files/wall.lt)
- [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py](moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py)
- [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py](moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py)
- [moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py](moltemplate/interpolate_curve.py)
- [moltemplate/pdbsort.py](moltemplate/pdbsort.py)
- [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py](tests/test_genpoly_lt.py)

</details>



`genpoly_lt.py` is a powerful utility within the moltemplate ecosystem that generates polymer structures in moltemplate (.lt) format. This tool reads coordinates from an input file and creates a sequence of moltemplate commands to build polymer molecules with monomers positioned at those coordinates, properly oriented along the polymer chain. The resulting output can be used directly with moltemplate.sh to build complex polymer systems for LAMMPS simulations.

For information about modifying existing polymers, see [genpoly_modify_lt.py](#3.2).

## Overview and Workflow

`genpoly_lt.py` serves as a bridge between geometric coordinate data and the moltemplate template system. It takes spatial coordinates that define the path of a polymer and converts them into a structured moltemplate file containing all the necessary commands to instantiate and position monomers along that path, create bonds between them, and properly orient them.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Data"
        coords["Coordinates File\n(coords.raw)"]
        sequence["Optional Sequence File\n(sequence.txt)"]
        helix["Optional Helix Angles\n(helix_angles.txt)"]
        orientations["Optional Orientations\n(orientations.txt)"]
    end

    subgraph "genpoly_lt.py Processing"
        readCoords["ReadCoords()\nParse coordinates"]
        readSeq["ReadSequence()\nParse monomer sequence"]
        directions["ChooseDirections()\nDetermine monomer orientations"]
        writeLT["WriteLTFile()\nGenerate .lt commands"]
    end

    subgraph "Output"
        ltFile["Polymer Definition\n(.lt file)"]
    end

    coords --> readCoords
    sequence --> readSeq
    readCoords --> directions
    readSeq --> writeLT
    directions --> writeLT
    helix --> writeLT
    orientations --> writeLT
    writeLT --> ltFile

    style readCoords fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333
    style readSeq fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333
    style directions fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333
    style writeLT fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:524-595](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:594-643](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:646-699](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:702-756]()

## Core Concepts

### Settings and Parameters

The `GPSettings` class manages all configurable aspects of polymer generation, including:

- Polymer and monomer names
- Bond definitions between monomers
- Angle, dihedral, and improper interactions
- Polymer circularity
- Helical parameters
- File paths for inputs

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GenPoly {
        +settings: GPSettings
        +coords_multi: List of coordinates
        +name_sequence_multi: List of monomer names
        +direction_vects: List of direction vectors
        +ParseArgs(argv)
        +ReadCoords(infile, ncolumns)
        +ReadSequence(infile)
        +ChooseDirections(coords)
        +WriteLTFile(outfile)
        +WritePolymer(outfile, name, coords, names, orientations, angles)
    }
    
    class GPSettings {
        +infile_name: String
        +direction_orig: List [1,0,0]
        +is_circular: Boolean
        +connect_ends: Boolean
        +delta_phi: Float
        +header: String
        +name_monomer: String
        +name_sequence_file: String
        +name_polymer: String
        +bonds_atoms: List
        +bonds_type: List
        +angles_atoms: List
        +angles_type: List
        +dihedrals_atoms: List
        +dihedrals_type: List
        +impropers_atoms: List
        +impropers_type: List
        +ParseArgs(argv)
    }
    
    GenPoly *-- GPSettings : contains
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:83-378](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:404-427]()

## Command Line Usage

The basic usage of `genpoly_lt.py` is:

```
genpoly_lt.py \
    [-polymer-name pname] \
    [-monomer-name mname] \
    [-sequence sequence.txt] \
    [-bond a1 a2] \
    [-bond btype a1 a2] \
    [-angle atype a1 a2 a3 i1 i2 i3] \
    [-dihedral dtype a1 a2 a3 a4 i1 i2 i3 i4] \
    [-improper itype a1 a2 a3 a4 i1 i2 i3 i4] \
    [-inherits ForceFieldObject] \
    [-header "import \"monomer.lt\""] \
    [-helix deltaphi] \
    [-axis x,y,z] \
    [-circular yes/no/connected] \
    [-cuts cuts.txt] \
    [-polymer-directions polarities.txt \
    [-dir-indices ia ib] \
    [-padding paddingX,paddingY,paddingZ] \
    < coords.raw > polymer.lt
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:34-57](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:35-58]()

### Key Command-Line Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `-polymer-name name` | Name of the moltemplate object to be created (default: "Polymer") |
| `-monomer-name name` | Name of the monomer to replicate along the polymer (default: "Monomer") |
| `-sequence file.txt` | File containing sequence of monomer types for heteropolymers |
| `-bond a1 a2` | Add a bond between atoms a1 and a2 in successive monomers |
| `-bond btype a1 a2` | Add a typed bond between atoms a1 and a2 in successive monomers |
| `-angle atype a1 a2 a3 i1 i2 i3` | Add angle interactions between atoms in different monomers |
| `-dihedral dtype a1 a2 a3 a4 i1 i2 i3 i4` | Add dihedral interactions between atoms in different monomers |
| `-improper itype a1 a2 a3 a4 i1 i2 i3 i4` | Add improper interactions between atoms in different monomers |
| `-inherits ForceField` | Make polymer inherit from a force field object |
| `-header "text"` | Add text at the beginning of the output file |
| `-helix angle` | Add helical twist (angle in degrees) between monomers |
| `-circular yes/no/connected` | Specify if polymer is circular |
| `-cuts file.txt` | Cut polymer to create multiple polymers |

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:62-357](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:125-378]()

## Working with Coordinates

### Input Format

The input coordinates file is a simple 3-column text file containing x, y, z coordinates for each monomer position:

```
x1 y1 z1
x2 y2 z2
x3 y3 z3
...
```

These coordinates define the positions where monomers will be placed. The `ReadCoords()` method parses this file and optionally splits the coordinates to create multiple polymers (if `-cuts` is specified).

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:524-590]()

### Monomer Orientation

One key feature of `genpoly_lt.py` is that it automatically orients monomers along the path of the polymer. The `ChooseDirections()` method calculates directional vectors for each monomer based on the positions of neighboring monomers:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input" 
        coord["Monomer Coordinates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        detect["Detect Direction\nCalculate vectors between positions"]
        calc["Calculate Orientations\nUse rotvv() to align monomers"]
        twist["Apply Twist\nAdd helical rotation if specified"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        orient["Oriented Monomers\nAlong polymer path"]
    end
    
    coord --> detect
    detect --> calc
    calc --> twist
    twist --> orient
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:646-699](), [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:766-848]()

## Polymer Structure Features

### Bonds Between Monomers

Bonds between monomers are specified using the `-bond` argument. For example:

```
-bond Backbone c2 c1
```

This creates bonds of type "Backbone" between atom "c2" in each monomer and atom "c1" in the following monomer. Multiple bonds can be added by using the `-bond` argument multiple times.

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:137-157](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:134-157]()

### Angles, Dihedrals, and Impropers

Similar to bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers can be specified between atoms in different monomers:

```
-angle AngleType a1 a2 a3 i1 i2 i3
```

Here, the atoms a1, a2, a3 are in monomers at relative positions i1, i2, i3 where:
- 0 corresponds to the current monomer
- 1 corresponds to the next monomer
- 2 corresponds to the monomer after that, etc.

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:158-217](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:160-210]()

### Circular Polymers

The `-circular` argument controls whether the polymer forms a closed loop:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Circular Options"
        direction TB
        no["no\nLinear polymer"]
        yes["yes\nCircular loop\nOriented to form ring"]
        connected["connected\nEnds connected\nNot orientation-adjusted"]
    end
    
    choice{"-circular argument"} --> no
    choice --> yes
    choice --> connected
```

When using `-circular yes`, the first and last monomers are connected with bonds, and their orientations are adjusted to point toward each other. With `-circular connected`, the ends are joined but orientations aren't adjusted, which is useful for periodic boundary conditions.

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:317-332](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:297-317]()

### Helical Structures

The `-helix` argument adds a twist along the polymer chain, rotating each monomer around its axis:

```
-helix 34.2857
```

This value is the angle in degrees that each monomer is rotated relative to the previous one, which is useful for creating helical structures like DNA.

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:333-338](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:282-295]()

## Creating Heteropolymers

For heteropolymers with varying monomer types, provide a sequence file with the `-sequence` argument:

```
-sequence sequence.txt
```

The sequence file should contain one monomer name per line, matching the total number of monomers in the polymer. For example:

```
CH3
CH2
CH2
CH3.rot(180,0,0,1)
```

Here, the polymer will have CH3 at both ends and CH2 in the middle, with the final CH3 rotated 180° to point in the opposite direction.

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:482-490](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:94-133]()

## Multiple Polymers

### Using Cuts

The `-cuts` argument allows creating multiple polymers from a single coordinate file:

```
-cuts cuts.txt
```

The cuts.txt file contains integers indicating where to cut the polymer. For example, if the cuts file contains "50 100", the coordinates will be split into three polymers: positions 0-49, 50-99, and 100-end.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Single Set of Coordinates"
        coords["Monomer Positions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cuts Processing"
        split["Split at specified positions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Multiple Polymers"
        poly1["Polymer 1"]
        poly2["Polymer 2"]
        poly3["Polymer 3"]
    end
    
    coords --> split
    split --> poly1
    split --> poly2
    split --> poly3
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:231-283](), [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:244-271]()

## Integration with Other Tools

### Using with interpolate_curve.py

`interpolate_curve.py` can be used to create smooth curves for polymer paths, which can then be fed into `genpoly_lt.py`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    startPoints["Initial Control Points"] --> interpolate["interpolate_curve.py\nGenerates smooth curve"]
    interpolate --> smoothCurve["Smoothed Coordinates"]
    smoothCurve --> genpoly["genpoly_lt.py\nGenerates polymer"]
    genpoly --> ltFile["Polymer .lt file"]
    ltFile --> moltemplate["moltemplate.sh\nGenerates LAMMPS files"]
```

This combination is particularly useful for creating polymers that follow complex paths, like DNA wrapping around histones or confined in specific geometries.

Sources: [doc/doc_interpolate_curve.md:36-44](), [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py:1-44]()

### Using with genpoly_modify_lt.py

After creating a polymer with `genpoly_lt.py`, you can use `genpoly_modify_lt.py` to modify specific regions of the polymer:

```
genpoly_modify_lt.py -polymer-name MyPolymer -length 100 -locations locations.txt -bond BondType a1 a2 0 1 >> polymer.lt
```

This allows adding specialized features at specific points along an existing polymer.

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_modify_lt.md:6-40](), [moltemplate/genpoly_modify_lt.py:7-57]()

## Python API

`genpoly_lt.py` can also be used as a Python module:

```python
import moltemplate

# Create a GenPoly object
gp = moltemplate.genpoly_lt.GenPoly()

# Set coordinates and monomer sequence
gp.coords_multi = [coordinates_list]
gp.name_sequence_multi = [monomer_names_list]

# Parse arguments for additional settings
gp.ParseArgs(['-helix', '34.2857',
              '-bond', 'Backbone', 'a1', 'a2',
              '-polymer-name', 'MyPolymer'])

# Generate an .LT file
import sys
gp.WriteLTFile(sys.stdout)
```

This approach allows programmatic control of polymer generation and integration with other Python code.

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:454-539](), [tests/test_genpoly_lt.py:1-44]()

## Data Flow Architecture

The following diagram shows the complete data flow through the `genpoly_lt.py` system:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Inputs"
        coords["Coordinates File\n(coords.raw)"]
        sequence["Sequence File\n(sequence.txt)"]
        cuts["Cuts File\n(cuts.txt)"]
        args["Command Line Arguments"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GenPoly Class"
        settings["GPSettings\nProcess arguments"]
        readCoords["ReadCoords()\nLoad coordinates"]
        readSeq["ReadSequence()\nLoad monomer types"]
        chooseDirs["ChooseDirections()\nCalculate orientations"]
        writeLT["WriteLTFile()\nGenerate output file"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        ltFile["Polymer Definition\n(.lt file)"]
    end
    
    coords --> readCoords
    sequence --> readSeq
    cuts --> settings
    args --> settings
    
    settings --> readCoords
    settings --> readSeq
    settings --> chooseDirs
    settings --> writeLT
    
    readCoords --> writeLT
    readSeq --> writeLT
    chooseDirs --> writeLT
    
    writeLT --> ltFile
```

Sources: [moltemplate/genpoly_lt.py:404-756]()

## Examples

### Simple Linear Polymer

```
genpoly_lt.py -bond Backbone c2 c1 \
               -monomer-name "Monomer" \
               -polymer-name "MyPolymer" \
               -header 'import "monomer.lt"' \
               < coords.raw > polymer.lt
```

### Circular DNA Model

```
genpoly_lt.py -circular yes -helix 34.2857 \
               -header 'import "basepair.lt"' \
               -monomer-name "BasePair" \
               -polymer-name "Plasmid" \
               -bond Backbone O3p_a P_a \
               -bond Backbone P_b O3p_b \
               < dna_basepair_coords.raw \
               > chromosome.lt
```

### Heteropolymer with Sequence

```
genpoly_lt.py -sequence sequence.txt \
               -bond Backbone c c \
               -polymer-name "Protein" \
               -header 'import "amino_acids.lt"' \
               < backbone_coords.raw > protein.lt
```

Sources: [doc/doc_genpoly_lt.md:425-450]()

## Common Use Cases

1. **DNA Simulation**: Creating coarse-grained or all-atom DNA models with helical structure
2. **Protein Folding**: Building protein structures from backbone coordinates
3. **Polymer Melts**: Generating multiple polymer chains for material simulations
4. **Confined Polymers**: Creating polymers that follow specific geometric constraints

`genpoly_lt.py` provides a versatile foundation for creating complex polymer structures that can be used in a wide range of molecular simulations with LAMMPS.

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the coarse-grained DNA models available in moltemplate and how to use them for molecular dynamics simulations. It focuses on two primary DNA models (3bp2p and 42bp3p), their properties, setup procedures, and applications in simulating various biological phenomena like DNA supercoiling and confinement. For information about all-atom simulations, see [All-Atom Simulations](#6.1), and for general polymer generation, see [genpoly_lt.py - Polymer Generation](#3.1).

## DNA Model Overview

Moltemplate provides coarse-grained DNA models that balance computational efficiency with biomolecular accuracy. These models accurately reproduce DNA geometry and mechanical properties while reducing computational demands compared to all-atom simulations.

### Types of DNA Models

#### The 3bp2p Model (3 base pairs = 2 particles)

This model represents 3 base pairs of DNA with 2 coarse-grained particles. It features:

- Double-helical conformation with major and minor grooves
- The ability to bend arbitrarily far without kinking
- Stable simulation with relatively large timesteps
- Accurate mechanical properties matching experimental measurements

#### The 42bp3p Model (42 base pairs = 3 particles)

This more aggressive coarse-graining approach represents 42 base pairs with 3 particles:

- Suitable for larger DNA structures (chromosomes, nucleoids)
- Maintains correct mechanical properties despite extreme coarse-graining
- Uses non-linear springs for bending and torsional stiffness
- Especially designed for supercoiling simulations

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/simple_dna_example/README.md:1-97]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/twistable_Kratky-Porod/42bp_3particles/twist_motor_supercoiling/README.md:1-29]()

## DNA Model Architecture

### Model Structure and Parameters

The DNA models use a system of connected particles with specific force field parameters to accurately represent DNA behavior.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "3bp2p Model"
        direction LR
        3bp["3 base pairs"] --> 2p["2 particles"]
        2p --> ModelA["Double-helical structure"]
        ModelA --> Props1["- Persistence length: 48.7nm
                         - Torsional persistence: 109.9nm
                         - Helical twist: 34.3° per bp
                         - Axial distance: 0.33nm per bp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "42bp3p Model"
        direction LR
        42bp["42 base pairs"] --> 3p["3 particles"]
        3p --> ModelB["Double-helical structure"]
        ModelB --> Props2["- Non-linear springs
                         - Infinite stiffness at 60° bending
                         - Infinite stiffness at 180° twisting"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Degrees of Freedom"
        direction LR
        DOF["Model parameters"] --> r1["r1 (distance)"]
        DOF --> r2["r2 (distance)"]
        DOF --> theta1["θ1 (angle)"]
        DOF --> theta2["θ2 (angle)"]
        DOF --> phib["φb (bend)"]
        DOF --> phit["φt (twist)"]
    end
```

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/simple_dna_example/README.md:9-32]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/twistable_Kratky-Porod/42bp_3particles/twist_motor_supercoiling/README.md:12-28]()

### Model Properties

The coarse-grained models accurately reproduce experimental DNA properties:

| Property | 3bp2p Model | Experimental | Reference |
|----------|-------------|--------------|-----------|
| Persistence length | 48.7101 nm | 46-48 nm | Kriegel et al. (2017) |
| Torsional persistence length | 109.9752 nm | 100-110 nm | Kriegel et al. (2017) |
| Helical twist per base-pair | 34.2599° | 34.3° | Sinden (1994) |
| Axial distance per base-pair | 0.32764 nm | 0.332 nm | Zwang et al. (2016) |

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/simple_dna_example/README.md:22-32]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/simple_dna_example/README.md:69-75]()

## Setting Up DNA Simulations

Creating DNA simulations involves several steps to generate the structure, apply the coarse-grained model, and set up the simulation conditions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Workflow for DNA Simulation Setup"
        direction TB
        A["1. Generate DNA Curve"] --> B["2. Process with interpolate_curve.py"]
        B --> C["3. Create polymer with genpoly_lt.py"]
        C --> D["4. Build system with moltemplate.sh"]
        D --> E["5. Run simulation with LAMMPS"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tools Used"
        direction TB
        T1["ndmansfield\n(random curve generator)"]
        T2["interpolate_curve.py\n(curve smoother)"]
        T3["genpoly_lt.py\n(polymer creator)"]
        T4["moltemplate.sh\n(system builder)"]
        T5["LAMMPS\n(simulation engine)"]
    end
    
    A -.-> T1
    B -.-> T2
    C -.-> T3
    D -.-> T4
    E -.-> T5
```

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:24-69]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/simple_dna_example/README.md:48-67]()

### Generating DNA Structures

DNA structures are typically created through these steps:

1. **Generate an initial curve** - Using tools like `ndmansfield` for random self-avoiding curves, or custom shapes for specific geometries
2. **Smooth and scale the curve** - Using `interpolate_curve.py` to prepare the curve for polymer generation
3. **Create the DNA polymer** - Using `genpoly_lt.py` to generate a moltemplate file with DNA along the curve
4. **Set up the full system** - Using `moltemplate.sh` to create LAMMPS input files

Example of curve generation and smoothing:

```bash
# Generate curve with ndmansfield
NMONOMERS=3058
B=0.996
Nx=11; Ny=11; Nz=11
./ndmansfield -box $Nx $Ny $Nz -seed 0 -tstart 1 -tsave 1000000 -tstop 1000000 > curve_lattice.txt

# Scale and smooth the curve
SCALE=$(echo "($NMONOMERS*$B)/($Nx*$Ny*$Nz-1)" | bc -l)
interpolate_curve.py $NMONOMERS $SCALE < curve_lattice.txt > curve_smooth.txt
```

Example of polymer generation with `genpoly_lt.py`:

```bash
# Create DNA polymer using the 3bp2p model
genpoly_lt.py -helix 102.7797 \
              -polymer-name 'DNAPolymer' \
              -monomer-name 'DNAMonomer' \
              -inherits 'DNAForceField' \
              -header 'import "dna_monomer.lt"' \
              -bond Backbone a a \
              -bond Backbone b b \
              -dihedral MajorGroove b b a a 0 1 1 2 \
              -dihedral Torsion a a b b 1 0 0 1 \
              -padding 20,20,20 \
              < curve_smooth.txt > dna_polymer.lt
```

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:34-69]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/twist_motor_supercoiling/README.md:58-73]()

## Advanced Simulation Features

### Twist Motors for DNA Supercoiling

Moltemplate supports "twist motors" that apply torque to DNA, simulating processes like DNA supercoiling by topoisomerases and gyrases in biological systems.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Twist Motor Implementation"
        direction LR
        DNA1["DNA segment"] --> Motor["Twist Motor"] --> DNA2["DNA segment"]
        Motor --> TorqueType["Torque Types"]
        TorqueType --> Constant["Constant Torque Motor"]
        TorqueType --> Rate["Constant Rate Motor"]
        
        Constant --> Effect1["Creates plectonemes\n(supercoiled DNA)"]
        Rate --> Effect2["Controls superhelical density"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Biological Parallel"
        direction LR
        BioProcess["Biological Processes"] --> Gyrase["DNA Gyrase"]
        BioProcess --> Topo["Topoisomerases"]
        BioProcess --> Replication["DNA Replication"]
        BioProcess --> Transcription["Transcription"]
    end
```

Twist motors are implemented using the `fix twist` command in LAMMPS, which needs to be specifically compiled with the LAMMPS source code. There are two types of twist motors:

1. **Constant torque motors** - Apply a fixed torque to DNA, causing supercoiling
2. **Constant rate motors** - Twist DNA at a consistent angular velocity

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/twist_motor_supercoiling/README.md:1-26]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/twistable_Kratky-Porod/42bp_3particles/twist_motor_supercoiling/README.md:1-46]()

### DNA Confinement Simulations

Moltemplate can simulate DNA confined within arbitrary shapes, such as viral capsids or bacterial cell volumes. The process typically involves:

1. Generating a DNA polymer within a small box
2. Placing that box inside the confinement structure
3. Simulating the relaxation of the DNA within the confined space

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "DNA Confinement Workflow"
        direction TB
        InitialDNA["Initial DNA\nconformation"] --> ConfineStruct["Confinement\nstructure"]
        ConfineStruct --> Relax["Relaxation\nsimulation"]
        Relax --> FinalStruct["Final\nconformation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Confinement Types"
        direction TB
        Viral["Viral capsid"]
        Cell["Bacterial cell"]
        Custom["Custom shape"]
    end
    
    ConfineStruct -.-> Viral
    ConfineStruct -.-> Cell
    ConfineStruct -.-> Custom
```

Special considerations for confinement simulations:
- For viral capsids, container particles are typically immobilized in the simulation
- Soft potentials are often necessary to allow the polymer to escape kinetic traps
- Wall-DNA interactions must be carefully parameterized

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:11-42]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:113-169]()

```mermaid
    end

        Packages --> EXTRA_MOLECULE["EXTRA-MOLECULE"]
        Packages --> EXTRA_PAIR["EXTRA-PAIR (42bp3p)"]
    end
    
    Model3bp2p -.-> MOLECULE
    Model3bp2p -.-> EXTRA_MOLECULE
    Model42bp3p -.-> MOLECULE
    Model42bp3p -.-> EXTRA_PAIR
    TwistMotors -.-> LAMMPS
```

## Example Applications

### Viral DNA Packaging

Simulate DNA confined in viral capsids, such as the HIV viral capsid:

- Demonstrates how to confine a polymer within an arbitrary shaped container
- Uses the 3bp2p model to represent DNA
- Initial DNA conformation is generated with `ndmansfield` and smoothed with `interpolate_curve.py`
- The viral capsid is represented by immobile particles
- Simulates the relaxation of DNA inside the confined space

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:1-42]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/confined_viral_DNA/README.md:124-169]()

### Bacterial Nucleoid Modeling

Simulate the entire bacterial chromosome (nucleoid):

- Uses the 42bp3p model to represent a 4Mbp circular DNA polymer
- Mimics the process of DNA relaxation and supercoiling during DNA replication
- Implements twist motors to create appropriate superhelical density
- Simulates DNA contraction during the replication process

The simulation workflow typically involves:
1. Creating an initially stretched circular DNA polymer
2. Applying twist to achieve proper supercoiling
3. Gradually relaxing tension by shortening the simulation box
4. Allowing the polymer to find its equilibrium conformation

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/twistable_Kratky-Porod/42bp_3particles/nucleoid_Ccrescentus_DNA_only/README.md:1-42]()
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/twistable_Kratky-Porod/42bp_3particles/nucleoid_Ccrescentus_DNA_only/README.md:72-119]()

## Prerequisites and Compilation Requirements

To run DNA simulations with these models, LAMMPS must be compiled with specific packages:

| Model | Required LAMMPS Packages | Additional Requirements |
|-------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| 3bp2p | MOLECULE, EXTRA-MOLECULE | None |
| 42bp3p | MOLECULE, EXTRA-PAIR | None |
| Twist Motors | MOLECULE, EXTRA-PAIR/EXTRA-MOLECULE | `fix_twist.cpp` and `fix_twist.h` from GitHub* |

*As of the documentation date, twist motor functionality requires downloading and manually adding the `fix_twist` files from the repository:
https://github.com/jewettaij/lammps/tree/fix_twist/src/USER-MISC

Sources:
- [examples/coarse_grained/DNA_models/dsDNA_only/2strands/3bp_2particles/README.md:17-24]()

This page documents the various file format converters in Moltemplate that allow importing external molecular data formats into the Moltemplate LT format. These converters form a crucial bridge between established molecular modeling software and Moltemplate's template-based approach to molecular simulation.

## Overview

Moltemplate supports multiple input pathways to transform external formats into its native LT format. These converters make it easier to integrate moltemplate with existing workflows and data from popular molecular modeling software.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "External Formats"
        MOL2["MOL2 Files"]
        AMBER["AMBER/GAFF Files"]
        OPLSAA["OPLSAA Files"]
        MSI["MSI/FRC Files"]
        LAMMPS["LAMMPS Input"]
    end
    
    subgraph "File Format Converters"
        mol22lt["mol22lt.py"]
        amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
        oplsaa2lt["oplsaa2lt.py"]
        msifrc2lt["msifrc2lt.py"]
        ltemplify["ltemplify.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate System"
        LT["LT Files"]
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
        output["LAMMPS Files"]
    end
    
    MOL2 --> mol22lt
    AMBER --> amber2lt
    OPLSAA --> oplsaa2lt
    MSI --> msifrc2lt
    LAMMPS --> ltemplify
    
    mol22lt --> LT
    amber2lt --> LT
    oplsaa2lt --> LT
    msifrc2lt --> LT
    ltemplify --> LT
    
    LT --> moltemplate
    moltemplate --> output
```

Sources: [moltemplate/__init__.py:41-45](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:1-594]()

## Conversion Process

The conversion process generally follows these steps:

1. Read the source file in its native format
2. Parse the molecular structure, atom types, charges, and parameters
3. Map these elements to Moltemplate's LT format
4. Generate an LT file that can be used in Moltemplate simulations

Each converter has specific considerations based on the source format, but they all share this basic workflow.

## Converter Types and Usage

### MOL2 to LT (mol22lt.py)

The `mol22lt.py` converter transforms MOL2 files (generated by tools like AmberTools, Gaussian, OpenBabel, or RED-server) into Moltemplate LT format. It extracts atomic coordinates, names, types, charges, and bonding information.

**Basic Usage:**
```bash
mol22lt.py --in molecule.mol2 --out molecule.lt [--name MOLECULE_NAME] [--ff FORCE_FIELD_NAME] [--ff-file FORCE_FIELD_FILE]
```

**Example:**
```bash
mol22lt.py --in benzene.mol2 --out benzene.lt --name Benzene --ff GAFF2 --ff-file gaff2.lt
```

**Extracted Information:**
- Charge (from MOL2 file or optional external file)
- Atom names and coordinates
- Atom types
- Subunit IDs and names
- Bond connectivity

**Diagram: MOL2 to LT Conversion Process**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MOL2["MOL2 File"] --> Parser["mol22lt Parser"]
    charges["Optional External\nCharges File"] --> Parser
    
    subgraph "Parsing Process"
        Parser --> AtomSection["Extract ATOM Section Data:
        - atom-names
        - XYZ coordinates
        - atom-types
        - subunit-id
        - charges"]
        
        Parser --> BondSection["Extract BOND Section Data:
        - atom1-atom2 connectivity"]
        
        AtomSection --> ProcessSubunits["Process Molecular Subunits"]
        BondSection --> ClassifyBonds["Classify Bonds (internal vs. between subunits)"]
    end
    
    ProcessSubunits --> Output["Generate LT File"]
    ClassifyBonds --> Output
    
    Output --> LT["Moltemplate LT File:
    - Molecule definition
    - Atom coordinates
    - Bond information
    - Force field assignments"]
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:1-322](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:75-492]()

**Limitations:**
- Does not work with MOL2 files containing multiple "chains"
- Atom names must be unique within each molecular subunit
- All atom-ID numbers and subunit-ID numbers must be unique and begin at 1

### AMBER/GAFF Conversion (amber2lt.py)

The `amber2lt.py` tool converts AMBER parameter and topology files to Moltemplate LT format. This provides a way to use AMBER and GAFF force fields with Moltemplate.

**Basic Usage:**
```bash
amber2lt.py --in param.frcmod --name MyForceField >> my_force_field.lt
```

**Workflow Example:**
```
# First create force field file from AMBER parameters
amber2lt.py --in benzene.frcmod --name MyForceField >> my_force_field.lt

# Then create molecule using mol22lt.py with this force field
mol22lt.py --in benzene.mol2 --out benzene.lt --name Benzene --ff MyForceField --ff-file my_force_field.lt
```

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:32-65]()

### OPLSAA Conversion (oplsaa2lt.py)

The `oplsaa2lt.py` converter transforms OPLSAA parameter files into Moltemplate LT format. It processes BOSS input files (.par, .sb) that contain the OPLSAA force field parameters.

**Basic Usage:**
```bash
oplsaa2lt.py --name OPLSAA --out oplsaa2024.lt --par oplsaa.par --sb oplsaa.sb
```

The converter handles special cases in OPLSAA typing, such as replacing problematic characters in atom type names and managing various bonded interaction redundancies.

**Implementation Details:**
- Parses atom definitions, charges, and masses
- Handles bond, angle, dihedral, and improper interactions
- Deals with duplicate types and parameters
- Includes water models

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Files"
        par["BOSS .par file\n(atoms, dihedrals, impropers)"]
        sb["BOSS .sb file\n(bonds, angles)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "oplsaa2lt.py"
        parse["Parse Force Field Files"]
        cleanup["Clean up Interaction Lists\n- Remove redundant entries\n- Manage duplicates\n- Sort by atom-type"]
        water["Add Water Models"]
        write["Write Moltemplate Format"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        lt["OPLSAA LT File"]
    end
    
    par --> parse
    sb --> parse
    parse --> cleanup
    cleanup --> water
    water --> write
    write --> lt
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:1-575](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md:1-53](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_classes.py:1-308]()

**Key Features:**
- Handles character conversions for OPLSAA types (e.g., "C:" → "C°", "C$" → "C^")
- Includes water models (TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, SPC/E, OPC)
- Supports force field specific symmetry rules for improper interactions

### MSI/BIOSYM Format Conversion (msifrc2lt.py)

The `msifrc2lt.py` tool converts MSI/BIOSYM/DISCOVERY force field files to Moltemplate LT format. This allows integration with these commercial simulation packages.

**Basic Usage:**
```bash
msifrc2lt.py --in forcefield.frc --out forcefield.lt
```

### LAMMPS Input Conversion (ltemplify.py)

The `ltemplify.py` tool converts existing LAMMPS input and data files into Moltemplate LT format. This is useful for converting existing LAMMPS simulations to use Moltemplate's template-based approach.

**Basic Usage:**
```bash
ltemplify.py system.data system.in.settings -name "SystemName" > system.lt
```

## Integration with Moltemplate Workflow

The file format converters integrate with the broader Moltemplate workflow, allowing users to move seamlessly between different molecular modeling tools.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Molecular Modeling Tools"
        amber["AmberTools/AMBER"]
        gauss["Gaussian"]
        ms["Materials Studio"]
        ob["OpenBabel"]
        red["RED Server"]
        existing["Existing LAMMPS Models"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate Converters"
        conv1["mol22lt.py"]
        conv2["amber2lt.py"]
        conv3["oplsaa2lt.py"]
        conv4["msifrc2lt.py"]
        conv5["ltemplify.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate System"
        lt["LT File Creation"]
        mt["moltemplate.sh"]
        ff["Force Field Assignment"]
        polygen["Polymer Generation\n(genpoly_lt.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Simulation"
        lammps["LAMMPS Simulation"]
    end
    
    amber --> |"MOL2, FRCMOD"| conv1
    amber --> |"Parameter Files"| conv2
    gauss --> |"MOL2"| conv1
    ms --> |"FRC Files"| conv4
    ob --> |"MOL2"| conv1
    red --> |"MOL2"| conv1
    existing --> conv5
    
    conv1 --> lt
    conv2 --> lt
    conv3 --> lt
    conv4 --> lt
    conv5 --> lt
    
    lt --> |"molecule.lt"| mt
    lt --> |"forcefield.lt"| ff
    ff --> mt
    polygen --> lt
    
    mt --> |"system.data\nsystem.in.*"| lammps
```

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:17-31](), [moltemplate/__init__.py:41-47]()

## Best Practices

### Choosing the Right Converter

1. **For small molecules with AMBER/GAFF force fields**:
   - Generate MOL2 and FRCMOD files using AmberTools
   - Use `amber2lt.py` to create a force field file
   - Use `mol22lt.py` to convert the molecule structure

2. **For OPLSAA force field parameters**:
   - Use `oplsaa2lt.py` with BOSS parameter files

3. **For existing LAMMPS simulations**:
   - Use `ltemplify.py` to convert LAMMPS files to LT format

### Important Considerations

#### Atomic Charges

- Many converters support extracting charges from the source files
- Some force fields (like COMPASS) have their own charge assignment rules
- User can also provide external charge files for `mol22lt.py`
- Verify charges are reasonable after conversion

#### Force Field Compatibility

- Ensure the force field parameters in the converted files are compatible with LAMMPS
- Some force fields require specific LAMMPS packages (e.g., AMBER requires the EXTRA-MOLECULE package)
- Check for missing parameters after conversion

#### Water Models

- Most force field converters include standard water models
- Special handling may be required for specific water models (TIP3P, TIP4P, SPC/E)

#### Improper Handling

- Different force fields use different improper angle conventions
- Moltemplate provides tools for handling these differences through symmetry rules

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:75-109](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md:10-29](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS/README.md:20-76]()

## Summary

The file format converters in Moltemplate provide a critical bridge between established molecular modeling software and Moltemplate's template-based approach. They enable users to leverage existing molecular structures and force field parameters while taking advantage of Moltemplate's powerful molecular building capabilities.

By converting various file formats to LT format, these tools allow users to:
- Import molecules from popular molecular modeling software
- Utilize established force fields (AMBER, GAFF, OPLSAA, DREIDING, COMPASS)
- Convert existing LAMMPS simulations to use Moltemplate's template-based approach
- Create complex molecular systems through Moltemplate's hierarchical molecule definition system

# mol22lt.py - MOL2 to LT Conversion

<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md)
- [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md)
- [examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS/README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS/README.md)
- [examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS/alkane_chain_single/moltemplate_files/system.lt](examples/all_atom/force_field_COMPASS/alkane_chain_single/moltemplate_files/system.lt)
- [examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md)
- [moltemplate/__init__.py](moltemplate/__init__.py)
- [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py)

</details>



The `mol22lt.py` program converts molecular structures in MOL2 format to moltemplate's LT format. This tool is part of moltemplate's input conversion subsystem, allowing molecular structures created in various molecular design programs to be used in LAMMPS simulations through moltemplate. For information about other conversion tools, see [File Format Converters](#4).

## Overview and Purpose

`mol22lt.py` creates LT files that define molecules based on the information extracted from MOL2 files (a widely used molecular structure format). This conversion is a critical step when:

1. Importing molecules designed in other software like AmberTools, Gaussian, OpenBabel, or RED-server
2. Converting complex molecules where manual creation of LT files would be impractical
3. Working with force fields like AMBER GAFF/GAFF2 where atom types in MOL2 files correspond to force field parameters

The program extracts coordinates, atom types, charges, bonds, and subunit information, preserving the molecular structure while transforming it into moltemplate's template-based format.

### Conversion Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "External Software"
        Ambertools["AmberTools"]
        Gaussian["Gaussian"]
        OpenBabel["OpenBabel"]
        RED["RED-server"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Files"
        MOL2[".mol2 File"]
        Charges["charges.txt\n(optional)"]
        FF["Force Field\n(optional)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "mol22lt Conversion"
        mol22lt["mol22lt.py"]
        ConvertMol22Lt["ConvertMol22Lt()\nFunction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        LT[".lt File"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate System"
        moltemplate["moltemplate.sh"]
        LAMMPS["LAMMPS Input Files"]
    end
    
    Ambertools --> MOL2
    Gaussian --> MOL2
    OpenBabel --> MOL2
    RED --> MOL2
    
    MOL2 --> mol22lt
    Charges --> mol22lt
    FF --> mol22lt
    
    mol22lt --> ConvertMol22Lt
    ConvertMol22Lt --> LT
    
    LT --> moltemplate
    moltemplate --> LAMMPS
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:3-7](), [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:69-73](), [moltemplate/__init__.py:41-42]()

## Command-Line Usage

The basic syntax for using `mol22lt.py` is:

```
mol22lt.py --in FILE.MOL2 --out FILE.LT [--name MOLECULE_NAME] [--charges charges.txt] [--ff FORCE_FIELD_NAME] [--ff-file FORCE_FIELD_FILE_NAME]
```

### Required Arguments

- `--in FILE.MOL2`: Specifies the MOL2 file to convert
- `--out FILE.LT`: Specifies the output LT file name

### Optional Arguments

- `--name MOLECULE_NAME`: Defines a name for the entire molecule (especially useful for multi-subunit molecules)
- `--charges charges.txt`: Provides custom charges from an external file
- `--ff FORCE_FIELD_NAME`: Specifies the force field name (e.g., GAFF2)
- `--ff-file FORCE_FIELD_FILE_NAME`: Specifies the force field file (e.g., gaff2.lt)
- `--upper-case-types`/`--lower-case-types`: Forces atom types to use upper/lowercase letters
- `--upper-case-names`/`--lower-case-names`: Forces atom names to use upper/lowercase letters

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:10-19](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:503-551]()

## Example Usage

Here's an example that converts a polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) polymer into moltemplate format:

```
mol22lt.py --in PPS_5mer.mol2 --out PPS_5mer.lt --name PPS5 --ff GAFF2 --ff-file "gaff2.lt"
```

After conversion, you can use the molecule in a moltemplate system file:

```
import "PPS_5mer.lt"
pps5_copy = new PPS5  # Create a single copy of the PPS5 polymer
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:22-35](), [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:414-431]()

## Data Extraction from MOL2 Files

The following information is extracted from the MOL2 file during conversion:

| MOL2 Section | Data Extracted | LT File Placement |
|--------------|----------------|-------------------|
| ATOM | Atom names (column 2) | `$atom:name` identifiers |
| ATOM | XYZ coordinates (columns 3,4,5) | Coordinates in Data Atoms section |
| ATOM | Atom types (column 6) | `@atom:type` references |
| ATOM | Subunit IDs (column 7) | Molecule organization |
| ATOM | Subunit names (column 8) | Molecule naming |
| ATOM | Charges (column 9) | Charge values in Data Atoms |
| BOND | Bond connections (columns 2,3) | Bond definitions |

The program ignores other sections of the MOL2 file and status information.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "MOL2 Format"
        MOL2_ATOM["@<TRIPOS>ATOM\nID name x y z type subID subName charge"]
        MOL2_BOND["@<TRIPOS>BOND\nID atom1 atom2 type"]
        MOL2_OTHER["Other MOL2 Sections\n(ignored)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ConvertMol22Lt Function"
        READ["Read MOL2 sections"]
        EXTRACT["Extract atom and bond data"]
        PROCESS["Process subunits"]
        CONVERT["Generate LT format"]
    end
    
    subgraph "LT Format Output"
        LT_HEADER["import statements\nMolecule definition"]
        LT_ATOMS["write(\"Data Atoms\") {\n  $atom:name $mol:id @atom:type charge x y z\n}"]
        LT_BONDS["write(\"Data Bond List\") {\n  $bond:id $atom:name1 $atom:name2\n}"]
        LT_USAGE["Usage instructions"]
    end
    
    MOL2_ATOM --> READ
    MOL2_BOND --> READ
    MOL2_OTHER --> READ
    
    READ --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> PROCESS
    PROCESS --> CONVERT
    
    CONVERT --> LT_HEADER
    CONVERT --> LT_ATOMS
    CONVERT --> LT_BONDS
    CONVERT --> LT_USAGE
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:75-94](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:114-212]()

## Handling Molecular Subunits

MOL2 files often contain multiple molecular subunits (designated by the subunit ID in column 7 of the ATOM section). `mol22lt.py` handles these in two ways:

1. **Default behavior**: Each subunit becomes a separate molecule definition in the LT file
2. **Using --name argument**: All subunits are grouped into a single molecule with the specified name

When creating multiple molecule definitions, the program ensures each has a unique name by adding suffixes if necessary.

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:123-131](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:222-281]()

## Force Field Integration

The atom type names in MOL2 files often correspond to force field types (like AMBER GAFF2). To use these force fields in your simulations:

1. Specify the force field name with `--ff` (e.g., `--ff GAFF2`)
2. Specify the force field file with `--ff-file` (e.g., `--ff-file gaff2.lt`)

This adds an import statement at the beginning of the generated LT file and makes the molecule inherit from the force field:

```
import "gaff2.lt"
PPS5 inherits GAFF2 {
  # Molecule definition
}
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:112-120](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:304-305]()

## Charges in Converted Molecules

By default, `mol22lt.py` reads charges from the MOL2 file (column 9 of the ATOM section). 

If the MOL2 file lacks charge information or you need to use different charges, you can provide a file containing the correct charges using the `--charges` argument. This file should contain one charge value per line, in the same order as atoms appear in the MOL2 file.

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:190-199](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:45-70](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:94-97](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:147-155]()

## Molecular Positioning

After conversion, you may need to adjust the position of the molecule. While `mol22lt.py` preserves the original coordinates, you can use moltemplate's `.move()` and `.rot()` commands to reposition the molecule:

```
PPS5.move(-24.7, -3.9, -4.3)  # Center the molecule at the origin
```

These commands can be added to the end of the LT file or used when instantiating the molecule in your system file.

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:152-168]()

## Working with Multiple Chains

`mol22lt.py` does not directly support MOL2 files containing multiple chains. However, you can use this workaround:

1. Split the MOL2 file into separate files, one per chain
2. Convert each file separately
3. Create a new LT file that combines the chains into a single complex

```
# Convert individual chain files
mol22lt.py --in chainA.mol2 --out chainA.lt --name ChainA --ff GAFF2 --ff-file "gaff2.lt"
mol22lt.py --in chainB.mol2 --out chainB.lt --name ChainB --ff GAFF2 --ff-file "gaff2.lt"

# Then create a file (protein_with_2_chains.lt) containing:
import "chainA.lt"  # Defines "ChainA"
import "chainB.lt"  # Defines "ChainB"
ProteinWith2Chains {
  a = ChainA
  b = ChainB
}
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:272-303]()

## Python API

You can use the `mol22lt.py` functionality directly within Python scripts:

```python
from moltemplate import ConvertMol22Lt

# Open the files
fMol2 = open('PPS_5mer.mol2', 'r')
fLT = open('PPS_5mer.lt', 'w')

# Perform the conversion
ConvertMol22Lt(fMol2,
               fLT,
               ff_name = 'GAFF2',        # Optional force field name
               ff_filename = 'gaff2.lt', # Optional force field file  
               object_name = 'PPS5')     # Optional molecule name
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:305-322](), [moltemplate/__init__.py:41]()

## Integration with Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "External Programs"

        Gaussian["Gaussian\nCharge calculation"]
    end

    end

    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate Files"
        FF_LT["Force Field LT\n(e.g., gaff2.lt)"]
        MOL_LT["Molecule LT"]
        SYSTEM_LT["System LT\n(simulation setup)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Simulation Files"
        DATA["system.data"]
        IN_SETTINGS["system.in.settings"]
        IN_INIT["system.in.init"]
    end
    
    RED --> MOL2
    AmberTools --> MOL2
    AmberTools --> FRCMOD
    Gaussian --> MOL2
```

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:25-30](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:32-43]()

## Limitations and Considerations

1. **Multiple Chains**: As noted above, MOL2 files with multiple chains require special handling.

2. **Atomic Charges**: Ensure your MOL2 file contains reasonable charges or provide them separately. For accurate simulations, charges should be calculated using appropriate methods (like those from RED-server, AmberTools, or Gaussian).

3. **Force Field Compatibility**: Ensure atom types in the MOL2 file match the force field you're using. This is especially important for AMBER/GAFF force fields.

4. **Bond Types**: By default, the tool does not include explicit bond types in the output, using a "Bond List" format instead. Bond type information from the MOL2 file is ignored.

5. **Experimental Status**: The documentation notes this software is experimental (as of 2024-12-05).

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:7](), [doc/doc_mol22lt.md:60-65](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:76-97](), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py:500]()

## Recommendations for Best Practice

1. **Charge Calculation**: Use dedicated tools like RED-server, AmberTools, or quantum chemistry software to calculate appropriate partial charges for your molecules.

2. **Force Field Selection**: Choose the appropriate force field for your simulation and ensure your MOL2 file uses compatible atom types.

3. **Molecule Inspection**: After conversion, inspect the generated LT file to ensure it properly represents your molecule.

4. **Multiple Chains**: For complex structures with multiple chains, follow the workaround described in the "Working with Multiple Chains" section.

5. **Position Adjustment**: Consider using `.move()` and `.rot()` commands to position your molecule appropriately in the simulation box.

Sources: [examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md:15-30](), [examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md:10-25]()

# Page: AMBER/GAFF Conversion

# AMBER/GAFF Conversion

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [doc/doc_amber2lt.md](doc/doc_amber2lt.md)
- [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_AMBER_files_to_LT_files/README.txt](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_AMBER_files_to_LT_files/README.txt)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt)
- [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff2.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/gaff2.lt)

</details>



## Overview

This page documents the process and tools for converting AMBER force field files (such as GAFF/GAFF2) into moltemplate format. The conversion enables molecular simulation workflows that originate with AMBER-based tools to seamlessly transition into LAMMPS simulations prepared with moltemplate. 

AMBER (Assisted Model Building with Energy Refinement) is a family of force fields commonly used for molecular dynamics of biomolecules, while GAFF (General AMBER Force Field) and GAFF2 are its extensions designed for small organic molecules. This document focuses specifically on the conversion process and not on the actual usage of these force fields - for information about using specific force fields in simulations, see [Force Fields](#5).

## Conversion Workflow

The conversion from AMBER force field files to moltemplate format is handled by the `amber2lt.py` script, which reads AMBER's `.dat` or `.frcmod` files and generates corresponding `.lt` files that can be used directly with moltemplate.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Files"
        gaff["GAFF Files (.dat)"]
        frcmod["FRCMOD Files (.frcmod)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Tool"
        amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        lt["Force Field Files (.lt)"]
    end
    
    gaff --> amber2lt
    frcmod --> amber2lt
    amber2lt --> lt
    
    lt --> usage["Use in moltemplate files"]
    
    classDef box fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    class "Input Files" box
    class "Conversion Tool" box
    class "Output Files" box
```

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:1-13](), [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:1-21]()

## The amber2lt.py Tool

The `amber2lt.py` script is the primary tool for converting AMBER/GAFF format files to moltemplate format. It extracts information about atom types, masses, bonds, angles, dihedrals, impropers, and non-bonded parameters from AMBER files and reformats them into moltemplate's syntax.

### Basic Usage

The basic command syntax for using `amber2lt.py` is:

```
amber2lt.py --in INPUT_FILE --name FORCE_FIELD_NAME [--out OUTPUT_FILE]
```

Where:
- `INPUT_FILE` is the AMBER format file to convert (e.g., gaff.dat)
- `FORCE_FIELD_NAME` is the name you want to assign to the force field in moltemplate
- `OUTPUT_FILE` is the optional name for the output LT file (defaults to stdout if omitted)

For example, to convert the GAFF force field file to moltemplate format:

```
amber2lt.py --in gaff.dat --name GAFF --out gaff.lt
```

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:797-816](), [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:10-29]()

### File Structure Conversion

The conversion process maps AMBER file sections to corresponding moltemplate sections:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "AMBER File Structure"
        a_mass["MASS Section"]
        a_bond["BOND Section"]
        a_angle["ANGLE Section"]
        a_dihedral["DIHEDRAL Section"]
        a_improper["IMPROPER Section"]
        a_pair["NONBONDED Section"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Process"
        extract["Extract Sections"]
        convert["Convert Parameters"]
        assemble["Assemble LT File"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate LT File"
        lt_mass["Data Masses"]
        lt_pair["Pair Coefficients"]
        lt_bond["Bond Coefficients"]
        lt_angle["Angle Coefficients"]
        lt_dihedral["Dihedral Coefficients"]
        lt_improper["Improper Coefficients"]
        lt_init["Init Settings"]
    end
    
    a_mass --> extract
    a_bond --> extract
    a_angle --> extract
    a_dihedral --> extract
    a_improper --> extract
    a_pair --> extract
    
    extract --> convert
    convert --> assemble
    
    assemble --> lt_mass
    assemble --> lt_pair
    assemble --> lt_bond
    assemble --> lt_angle
    assemble --> lt_dihedral
    assemble --> lt_improper
    assemble --> lt_init
    
    classDef box fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    class "AMBER File Structure" box
    class "Conversion Process" box
    class "Moltemplate LT File" box
```

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:699-762](), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:767-793]()

### Understanding the Conversion Process

The `amber2lt.py` script performs several key tasks during conversion:

1. **Section Extraction**: Identifies and extracts different sections from the AMBER file
2. **Parameter Formatting**: Converts AMBER parameter formats to LAMMPS-compatible formats
3. **Order Arrangement**: Sorts interactions with wildcards to ensure proper precedence
4. **File Generation**: Creates a structured LT file with all necessary components

The script handles specific AMBER conventions like wildcard atoms (`X`) and converts them to the proper syntax for moltemplate.

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:105-185](), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:189-227]()

## Generated Force Field Format

When `amber2lt.py` converts an AMBER force field file, it creates a structured LT file that defines the force field's parameters. This file includes several key sections:

### Atom Type Definitions

The generated file begins with comments describing the atom types defined in the force field, which helps users understand what atom types to assign to their molecules.

For example, from GAFF:

```
  #  @atom:c  Sp2 C carbonyl group
  #  @atom:c1  Sp C
  #  @atom:c2  Sp2 C
  #  @atom:c3  Sp3 C
  #  @atom:ca  Sp2 C in pure aromatic systems
```

### Mass Definitions

The `Data Masses` section defines the mass for each atom type:

```
  write_once("Data Masses") {
    @atom:c 12.01
    @atom:c1 12.01
    @atom:c2 12.01
    @atom:c3 12.01
    @atom:ca 12.01
    ...
  }
```

### Interaction Parameters

The file includes sections for all interaction parameters, such as pair coefficients:

```
  write_once("In Settings") {
    pair_coeff @atom:c @atom:c lj/charmm/coul/long 0.0860 3.3996695084235347
    pair_coeff @atom:c1 @atom:c1 lj/charmm/coul/long 0.2100 3.3996695084235347
    ...
  }
```

And similar sections for bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers:

```
  write_once("In Settings") {
    bond_coeff @bond:c-c harmonic 291.7 1.5482
    ...
  }
  
  write_once("Data Bonds By Type") {
    @bond:c-c @atom:c @atom:c
    ...
  }
```

### Initialization Settings

The file ends with initialization settings that define the overall simulation parameters:

```
  write_once("In Init") {
    # Default styles and settings for AMBER based force-fields:
    units           real
    atom_style      full
    bond_style      hybrid harmonic
    angle_style     hybrid harmonic
    dihedral_style  hybrid fourier
    improper_style  hybrid cvff
    pair_style      hybrid lj/charmm/coul/long 9.0 10.0 10.0
    kspace_style    pppm 0.0001
    
    pair_modify     mix arithmetic
    special_bonds   amber
  }
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt:58-155](), [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt:157-226](), [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt:228-311](), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:722-743]()

## Using Converted Force Fields

After converting an AMBER force field to moltemplate format, you can use it in your molecular simulations. Here's how:

### Importing Force Fields

To use a converted force field in your moltemplate files, you simply import it at the beginning of your molecule definition:

```
import "gaff.lt"

Benzene inherits GAFF {
  # molecule definition here
}
```

### Inheriting Force Field Parameters

When defining a molecule, you use the `inherits` keyword to apply the force field parameters to your molecule:

```
Benzene inherits GAFF {
  write('Data Atoms') {
    $atom:c1  $mol  @atom:ca  -0.115   -0.739   1.189  -0.00733
    $atom:c2  $mol  @atom:ca  -0.115    0.614   1.208   0.35167
    # more atoms...
  }
  
  write("Data Bond List") {
    $bond:b1 $atom:c1 $atom:c2
    # more bonds...
  }
}
```

The `@atom:ca` syntax in the atom definition references the GAFF atom type for aromatic carbon, which brings in all associated parameters from the force field.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt:13-25](), [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:32-46]()

## Integration with MOL2 Files and AmberTools

A common workflow involves:
1. Using AmberTools to prepare MOL2 files with proper atom typing and charges
2. Converting AMBER force field files to LT format with `amber2lt.py`
3. Converting MOL2 files to LT format with `mol22lt.py`
4. Using these files together in moltemplate

This workflow is illustrated below:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "AmberTools"
        antechamber["antechamber"]
        parmchk["parmchk2"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Files"
        mol["Initial Structure"]
        gaff_dat["gaff.dat"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Intermediate Files"
        mol2["Molecule.mol2"]
        frcmod["Molecule.frcmod"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Tools"
        amber2lt["amber2lt.py"]
        mol22lt["mol22lt.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        ff_lt["force_field.lt"]
        mol_lt["molecule.lt"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Moltemplate"
        run["moltemplate.sh"]
        lammps["LAMMPS Input Files"]
    end
    
    mol --> antechamber
    antechamber --> mol2
    mol2 --> parmchk
    parmchk --> frcmod
    
    gaff_dat --> amber2lt
    frcmod --> amber2lt
    amber2lt --> ff_lt
    
    mol2 --> mol22lt
    ff_lt --> mol22lt
    mol22lt --> mol_lt
    
    ff_lt --> run
    mol_lt --> run
    run --> lammps
    
    classDef box fill:none,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    class "AmberTools" box
    class "Input Files" box
    class "Intermediate Files" box
    class "Conversion Tools" box
    class "Output Files" box
    class "Moltemplate" box
```

Sources: [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:50-85](), [moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt:26-52]()

## Advanced Uses and Considerations

### Handling Multiple Molecules

When working with multiple molecules that require the same force field:

1. Convert the AMBER force field once to create your base `.lt` file
2. For each molecule, use `mol22lt.py` to convert its MOL2 file to LT format
3. Import the same force field file in each molecule's LT file

This approach ensures consistent force field parameters across all your molecules.

### Dealing with Custom Parameters

If you have custom or modified parameters in a FRCMOD file:

1. Convert your base force field (e.g., GAFF) to LT format
2. Convert your FRCMOD file to LT format
3. Import both files in your molecule definition, with the custom parameters imported last to override the base parameters

### Handling Wildcard Atoms

AMBER force fields often use wildcard atoms (`X`) to represent any atom type in interaction parameters. The `amber2lt.py` script handles these wildcards by:

1. Converting them to the `*` wildcard syntax in moltemplate
2. Sorting interaction parameters so that more specific interactions (without wildcards) take precedence over generic ones (with wildcards)

```
# AMBER format:
X -CA-CA-X    4   14.50        180.0             2.         intrpol.bsd.on C6H6

# Converted to moltemplate format:
dihedral_coeff @dihedral:X-CA-CA-X fourier 1 14.50 180.0 2.0     # intrpol.bsd.on C6H6
```

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:512-524](), [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:117-141]()

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

### Section Extraction Failures

Sometimes `amber2lt.py` may fail to correctly identify sections in AMBER files. If this occurs, you can manually extract sections and provide them as separate inputs:

```
amber2lt.py --name FORCE_FIELD_NAME \
           --mass mass.txt \
           --bond bond.txt \
           --angle angle.txt \
           --dihedral dihedral.txt \
           --improper improper.txt \
           --pair pair.txt \
           --out FORCE_FIELD.lt
```

### Conversion Parameter Issues

AMBER uses different conventions for Lennard-Jones parameters than LAMMPS. The `amber2lt.py` script accounts for these differences by:

1. Converting AMBER's atom radii (which is 0.5*sigma) to full sigma values for LAMMPS
2. Adjusting the parameters to account for different energy function forms

If you encounter issues with converted parameters, check the conversion logic in the `ConvertPair2Lt` function.

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py:633-691](), [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:129-141]()

## Using the Python API

You can also use `amber2lt.py` as a Python module to perform conversions programmatically:

```python
import moltemplate
# Open the file you want to convert
with open('gaff.dat', 'r') as file_in:
    lines_in = file_in.readlines()
# Now create a new moltemplate file
lines_out = ConvertAmber2Lt(object_name, lines_in)
# Write the contents of the new file
with open('gaff.lt', 'w') as file_out:
    file_out.write(''.join(output_lines))
```

For more granular control, you can also use `ConvertAmberSections2Lt()` if you have already extracted the different sections of the file.

Sources: [doc/doc_amber2lt.md:143-168]()

## Conclusion

The `amber2lt.py` tool provides a streamlined way to convert AMBER force field files to moltemplate format, enabling seamless integration of AMBER-based workflows with LAMMPS simulations prepared through moltemplate. This conversion preserves all the force field parameters while reformatting them to be compatible with moltemplate's syntax and LAMMPS' requirements.

---

# OPLSAA Conversion

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_utils.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_utils.py)

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the `oplsaa2lt.py` system, which converts OPLSAA (Optimized Potentials for Liquid Simulations All-Atom) force field files from BOSS format (`.par` and `.sb` files) to moltemplate format (`.lt` files). The converted force field can then be used with the moltemplate system to define molecules for LAMMPS molecular dynamics simulations. For information about using the resulting force field in simulations, see [Force Fields](#5) and [OPLSAA Force Field](#5.1).

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md:1-32](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:1-22]()

## System Overview

The OPLSAA conversion tool takes BOSS parameter files as input and generates a moltemplate-compatible file that defines the OPLSAA force field for use in LAMMPS simulations. The conversion process handles atom types, bonded interactions (bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers), and adds additional water models.

### OPLSAA Conversion Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Files"
        par[".par file\n(Atoms, Dihedrals, Impropers)"]
        sb[".sb file\n(Bonds, Angles)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "oplsaa2lt.py Conversion Process"
        parse_sb["parse_bond_line\nparse_angle_line"]
        parse_par["parse_atom_line\nget_dihedrals_and_impropers"]
        clean["Cleanup & Processing\n- Delete redundant entries\n- Handle duplicates\n- Sort by type"]
        water["Add Water Models\n- TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P\n- SPC, SPC/E, OPC"]
        write["Generate Output File"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        lt["OPLSAA Force Field (.lt)\n- Atom types and charges\n- Bonds, Angles, Dihedrals, Impropers\n- Water models"]
    end
    
    par --> parse_par
    sb --> parse_sb
    
    parse_sb --> clean
    parse_par --> clean
    
    clean --> water
    water --> write
    
    write --> lt
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:319-572](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md:1-53]()

## Key Components

The OPLSAA conversion system consists of three main Python files that work together to handle the conversion process:

1. `oplsaa2lt.py` - Main script that coordinates the conversion process
2. `oplsaa2lt_classes.py` - Defines the data structures used in the conversion
3. `oplsaa2lt_utils.py` - Provides utility functions and constants

### Class Hierarchy and Data Model

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Atom {
        +int type_id
        +int atomic_number
        +str type_str
        +str charge
        +str sigma
        +str epsilon
        +str element
        +str mass
        +str comment
        +type_long()
        +charge_line()
        +mass_line()
        +repl_line()
        +nb_line()
    }
    
    class BondedInteraction {
        <<abstract>>
        +list types
        +str comment
        +int duplicate_count
        +bool to_skip
        +bool to_comment
        +typename()
        +sort_key()
        +coeff_line()* 
        +bytype_line()*
    }
    
    class Bond {
        +str k
        +str eq
        +coeff_line()
        +bytype_line()
    }
    
    class Angle {
        +str k
        +str eq
        +coeff_line()
        +bytype_line()
    }
    
    class Dihedral {
        +str v1
        +str v2
        +str v3
        +str v4
        +coeff_line()
        +bytype_line()
    }
    
    class Improper {
        +str v1
        +str v2
        +str v3
        +str v4
        +coeff_line()
        +bytype_line()
    }
    
    BondedInteraction <|-- Bond
    BondedInteraction <|-- Angle
    BondedInteraction <|-- Dihedral
    BondedInteraction <|-- Improper
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_classes.py:1-308]()

## Command Line Usage

The `oplsaa2lt.py` script requires command line arguments to specify the input and output files:

```
./oplsaa2lt.py --name OPLSAA --out oplsaa2024.lt \
  --par oplsaa.par \
  --sb  oplsaa.sb
```

Where:
- `--name` specifies the name of the moltemplate object to create (default: "OPLSAA")
- `--out` specifies the name of the output .lt file
- `--par` specifies the BOSS .par file containing atom, dihedral, and improper information
- `--sb` specifies the BOSS .sb file containing bond and angle information

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md:6-26](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:320-350]()

## Detailed Conversion Process

### Type Conversion

The OPLSAA format contains atom type names with characters that are problematic for moltemplate. The system converts these characters to compatible alternatives:

```
C:  → C°   # moltemplate doesn't like :
C$  → C^   # $ is used by moltemplate
N$  → N^   # $ is used by moltemplate
O$  → O^   # $ is used by moltemplate
C#  → C|   # moltemplate doesn't like #
N*  → N§   # N* would create problems in bonded interactions
C(O) → C⟮  # moltemplate doesn't like "(" or ")", but "⟮" is okay
```

The wildcards "X", "Y", "Z" in BOSS files are converted to "??" for moltemplate, and single-character types are padded to ensure they are 2 characters long (e.g., "C" → "C~").

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:26-58]()

### Parsing Input Files

The system parses the BOSS input files using dedicated functions:

1. `.sb` file parsing:
   - `parse_bond_line()` - Extracts bond parameters
   - `parse_angle_line()` - Extracts angle parameters
   - `get_bonds_and_angles()` - Processes the entire file

2. `.par` file parsing:
   - `parse_atom_line()` - Extracts atom type information
   - `get_dihedrals_and_impropers()` - Extracts dihedral and improper parameters

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:61-168]()

### Handling Duplicates and Redundancy

OPLSAA files often contain redundant entries and duplicates that need special handling:

1. `delete_redundant_duplicates()` - Removes truly redundant entries
2. `count_nonredundant_duplicates()` - Identifies and counts duplicate entries that have different parameters
3. `sort_duplicates()` - Sorts duplicate interactions to ensure the most general ones appear last (giving them higher priority in moltemplate)

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:171-316]()

### Water Models

The system adds several water models that are not fully specified in the original OPLSAA files:

- TIP3P
- TIP4P
- TIP5P
- SPC/SPC-E
- OPC

For each model, it defines the atom types with appropriate charges, sigma, and epsilon values, as well as the necessary bond and angle parameters.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:389-457]()

## Output File Structure

The generated .lt file contains the following sections:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ltfile["OPLSAA Force Field (.lt file)"]
    ltfile --> header["Header Section\n- File metadata\n- Type conversion notes\n- Water model notes"]
    ltfile --> charges["In Charges Section\n- Atom partial charges"]
    ltfile --> masses["Data Masses Section\n- Atom masses"]
    ltfile --> equiv["Type Equivalences\n- Atom type mappings"]
    ltfile --> nb["Non-Bonded Interactions\n- pair_coeffs"]
    ltfile --> bond["Bond Interactions\n- bond_coeffs\n- Data Bonds By Type"]
    ltfile --> angle["Angle Interactions\n- angle_coeffs\n- Data Angles By Type"]
    ltfile --> dihedral["Dihedral Interactions\n- dihedral_coeffs\n- Data Dihedrals By Type"]
    ltfile --> improper["Improper Interactions\n- improper_coeffs\n- Data Impropers By Type"]
    ltfile --> init["In Init Section\n- LAMMPS simulation settings"]
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:460-571](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_utils.py:3-132]()

## Improper Handling

Improper interactions in OPLSAA require special treatment. The system follows the OPLS convention where the central atom is the third atom in the interaction. The `cenKswapIL.py` file in the `nbody_alt_symmetry` directory provides the rules for generating improper interactions in the OPLS force field.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Improper Interaction Structure"
        a0["Atom 0"]
        a1["Atom 1"] 
        a2["Atom 2 (Central)"]
        a3["Atom 3"]
        
        a2 --- a0
        a2 --- a1
        a2 --- a3
    end
```

The canonical ordering of atoms in an improper interaction is important to avoid redundancy. The system implements a canonical ordering that ensures consistent representation of improper interactions.

Sources: [moltemplate/nbody_alt_symmetry/cenKswapIL.py:1-77](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py:143-168]()

## Usage Example

After conversion, the resulting .lt file can be used to define molecules in moltemplate:

```
import "oplsaa2024.lt"

Ethylene inherits OPLSAA {
  # atom-id mol-id atom-type charge   X       Y       Z     # comment
  write('Data Atoms') {
    $atom:c1  $mol @atom:143  0.00 -0.6695   0.00000  0.000  #143<->"alkene C (H2-C=)"
    $atom:h11 $mol @atom:144  0.00 -1.23422 -0.85446  0.000  #144<->"alkene H (H-C=)"
    # Additional atoms...
  }
  # BondID     AtomID1  AtomID2
  write('Data Bond List') {
    $bond:c1h1 $atom:c1 $atom:h11
    # Additional bonds...
  }
} # Ethylene
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md:26-44](), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_utils.py:3-43]()

## Integration with Moltemplate

The generated OPLSAA force field integrates with the rest of moltemplate through the inheritance mechanism. The force field object defines atom types, charges, and interaction parameters, while user-defined molecule objects inherit these properties and add specific geometries.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    oplsaa["OPLSAA Force Field\n(.lt file)"]
    
    subgraph "User-defined Molecules"
        mol1["Molecule 1\ninherits OPLSAA"]
        mol2["Molecule 2\ninherits OPLSAA"]
        mol3["Molecule 3\ninherits OPLSAA"]
    end
    
    oplsaa --> mol1
    oplsaa --> mol2
    oplsaa --> mol3
    
    mol1 --> lammps["LAMMPS Input Files\n- system.data\n- system.in.settings\n- system.in.charges\n- system.in.init"]
    mol2 --> lammps
    mol3 --> lammps
    
    lammps --> simulation["LAMMPS Simulation"]
```

The moltemplate system uses the OPLSAA force field parameters to generate the necessary LAMMPS input files for simulation.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt_utils.py:107-132]()
